description: Cyclic dimer of lactic acid; its ring-opening polymerization is the main route to PLA.

name: 1,4-Butanediol
description: Four-carbon diol used with terephthalic acid to make PBT and in polyurethanes.

name: Maleic anhydride
description: Cyclic anhydride used in unsaturated polyester resins for fiberglass boats and panels.

name: Phthalic anhydride
description: Aromatic anhydride used to make alkyd paint resins and phthalate plasticizers.

name: Dichlorodimethylsilane
description: Hydrolyzes and condenses to polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), the backbone of silicone rubber.

name: N-Vinylpyrrolidone
description: Monomer of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), a binder in tablets, hair gels and adhesives.

name: 1,3,5-Trioxane
description: Cyclic trimer of formaldehyde, polymerized to polyoxymethylene (POM, acetal) plastic.

name: Ethyl cyanoacrylate
description: The monomer in superglue; traces of water start its rapid anionic polymerization.

name: 11-Aminoundecanoic acid
description: Castor-oil-derived amino acid that self-condenses to nylon 11 for fuel lines and tubing.

name: Laurolactam
description: Twelve-carbon lactam that ring-opens to nylon 12, used in tubing and 3D printing powder.

name: p-Phenylenediamine
description: Aromatic diamine that condenses with terephthaloyl chloride to make Kevlar aramid fiber.

name: Terephthaloyl chloride
description: Diacyl chloride partner of p-phenylenediamine in making Kevlar and Twaron aramids.

name: 4,4'-Oxydianiline
description: Ether-linked diamine that reacts with pyromellitic dianhydride to form Kapton polyimide.

name: Pyromellitic dianhydride
description: Aromatic dianhydride that forms heat-resistant polyimides such as Kapton film.

name: Alanine (Ala, A)
description: Small nonpolar proteinogenic amino acid; carries nitrogen from muscle to liver in the glucose-alanine cycle.

name: Arginine (Arg, R)
description: Basic proteinogenic amino acid with a guanidinium group; precursor of nitric oxide, urea and creatine.

name: Asparagine (Asn, N)
description: Polar amide amino acid in proteins; the attachment site for N-linked glycans on glycoproteins.

name: Aspartic acid (Asp, D)
description: Acidic proteinogenic amino acid; donates nitrogen in the urea cycle and in purine and pyrimidine synthesis.

name: Cysteine (Cys, C)
description: Thiol-bearing amino acid that forms disulfide bridges in proteins and supplies sulfur to glutathione.

name: Glutamic acid (Glu, E)
description: Acidic amino acid central to nitrogen metabolism and the main excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain.

name: Glutamine (Gln, Q)
description: Most abundant free amino acid in blood; carries nitrogen between tissues and fuels dividing cells.

name: Glycine (Gly, G)
description: Simplest amino acid, with no side chain; common in collagen and an inhibitory neurotransmitter in the spinal cord.

name: Histidine (His, H)
description: Imidazole-bearing amino acid that often acts as a proton shuttle in enzyme active sites; precursor of histamine.

name: Isoleucine (Ile, I)
description: Essential branched-chain amino acid with two stereocenters; hydrophobic residue in protein cores.

name: Leucine (Leu, L)
description: Essential branched-chain amino acid; a hydrophobic residue and a signal that switches on muscle protein synthesis.

name: Lysine (Lys, K)
description: Essential basic amino acid with a primary amine side chain; a key site of acetylation on histone proteins.

name: Methionine (Met, M)
description: Essential sulfur amino acid; the start residue of nearly every protein and the precursor of S-adenosylmethionine.

name: Phenylalanine (Phe, F)
description: Essential aromatic amino acid with a benzyl side chain; converted to tyrosine in the liver.

name: Proline (Pro, P)
description: Cyclic amino acid whose ring locks the backbone; abundant in collagen and common at turns in proteins.

name: Serine (Ser, S)
description: Hydroxyl amino acid; the nucleophile in serine proteases and a frequent phosphorylation site.

name: Threonine (Thr, T)
description: Essential hydroxyl amino acid with two stereocenters; a site of phosphorylation and O-linked glycosylation.

name: Tryptophan (Trp, W)
description: Essential amino acid with an indole side chain; precursor of serotonin, melatonin and niacin.

name: Tyrosine (Tyr, Y)
description: Aromatic phenol amino acid; precursor of dopamine, adrenaline, thyroid hormones and melanin.

name: Valine (Val, V)
description: Essential branched-chain amino acid with an isopropyl side chain; hydrophobic residue in proteins.

name: Selenocysteine (Sec, U)
description: The 21st amino acid, cysteine with selenium in place of sulfur; found in glutathione peroxidase and other enzymes.

name: Pyrrolysine (Pyl, O)
description: The 22nd amino acid, a lysine with a pyrroline ring; encoded by UAG in some methane-producing archaea.

name: Ornithine
description: Non-proteinogenic amino acid that carries the urea cycle; precursor of polyamines such as putrescine.

name: Citrulline
description: Urea cycle intermediate formed from ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate; named after watermelon (Citrullus).

name: Taurine
description: Aminosulfonic acid abundant in heart, muscle and retina; conjugates bile acids and helps regulate cell volume.

name: beta-Alanine
description: Beta amino acid with the amine on the third carbon; building block of carnosine and of pantothenic acid.

name: Sarcosine
description: N-methylglycine, an intermediate of choline and glycine metabolism found in muscle and other tissues.

name: 4-Hydroxyproline
description: Proline hydroxylated after translation; stabilizes the collagen triple helix and requires vitamin C to form.

name: D-Alanine
description: Mirror-image form of alanine; a component of bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan and the target of vancomycin.

name: D-Serine
description: D form of serine made by brain cells; a co-agonist at NMDA glutamate receptors.

name: Homocysteine
description: Sulfur amino acid formed from methionine; recycled with folate and vitamin B12 or converted to cysteine.

name: Cystine
description: Two cysteines joined by a disulfide bond; the oxidized form found in blood and in kidney stones in cystinuria.

name: Homoserine
description: Non-proteinogenic amino acid; intermediate in bacterial and plant synthesis of threonine and methionine.

name: Carnitine
description: Quaternary ammonium compound that carries long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for beta-oxidation.

name: Creatine
description: Guanidino compound made from arginine and glycine; stores high-energy phosphate in muscle and brain.

name: Theanine
description: Glutamine analog with an N-ethyl amide, found almost only in tea leaves; gives green tea its savory taste.

name: Pyroglutamic acid
description: Cyclic lactam of glutamic acid; found at the N-terminus of many peptides and in the glutathione cycle.

name: Kynurenine
description: Main breakdown product of tryptophan in the kynurenine pathway that leads to NAD+ synthesis.

name: Canavanine
description: Arginine analog made by legumes such as jack bean; toxic to insects when built into proteins.

name: Ergothioneine
description: Sulfur-containing histidine derivative made by fungi and bacteria; accumulated by humans as an antioxidant.

name: Glycine betaine
description: Trimethylglycine; an osmolyte in plants and microbes and a methyl donor in human homocysteine metabolism.

name: 2-Aminoisobutyric acid
description: Non-proteinogenic amino acid found in meteorites and fungal peptides; strongly favors helical peptide shapes.

name: Adenine
description: Purine nucleobase that pairs with thymine in DNA and uracil in RNA; part of ATP, NAD+ and coenzyme A.

name: Guanine
description: Purine nucleobase that pairs with cytosine through three hydrogen bonds in DNA and RNA.

name: Cytosine
description: Pyrimidine nucleobase that pairs with guanine; its methylation regulates gene expression.

name: Thymine
description: Pyrimidine nucleobase, 5-methyluracil, found in DNA where it pairs with adenine.

name: Uracil
description: Pyrimidine nucleobase of RNA that takes the place of thymine and pairs with adenine.

name: Hypoxanthine
description: Purine base formed by deamination of adenine; found in inosine and recycled by the salvage pathway.

name: Xanthine
description: Purine base formed from hypoxanthine and guanine; oxidized to uric acid by xanthine oxidase.

name: 5-Methylcytosine
description: Methylated cytosine at CpG sites in DNA; an epigenetic mark that silences genes.

name: 5-Hydroxymethylcytosine
description: Oxidized 5-methylcytosine made by TET enzymes; an intermediate in active DNA demethylation.

name: Inosine
description: Nucleoside of hypoxanthine and ribose; at the tRNA wobble position it pairs with several bases.

name: Adenosine
description: Nucleoside of adenine and ribose; a signaling molecule that promotes sleep and dilates blood vessels.

name: Guanosine
description: Nucleoside of guanine and ribose; a building block of RNA after phosphorylation.

name: Cytidine
description: Nucleoside of cytosine and ribose; a component of RNA and of CDP-activated lipid precursors.

name: Thymidine
description: Deoxyribonucleoside of thymine; found only in DNA and used to label dividing cells.

name: Uridine
description: Nucleoside of uracil and ribose; part of RNA and of UDP-sugars used to build glycogen.

name: Deoxyadenosine
description: Adenine nucleoside with 2'-deoxyribose; a building block of DNA.

name: Deoxyguanosine
description: Guanine nucleoside with 2'-deoxyribose; a building block of DNA and a common oxidation target.

name: Deoxycytidine
description: Cytosine nucleoside with 2'-deoxyribose; a building block of DNA.

name: Pseudouridine
description: Isomer of uridine with a C-C sugar bond; the most common modified nucleoside in RNA.

name: 7-Methylguanosine
description: Methylated guanosine that forms the 5' cap of eukaryotic messenger RNA.

name: Adenosine monophosphate (AMP)
description: Adenine ribonucleotide with one phosphate; an RNA monomer and a signal of low cell energy.

name: Adenosine diphosphate (ADP)
description: Adenine nucleotide with two phosphates; phosphorylated to ATP by ATP synthase.

name: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP)
description: Main energy carrier of the cell; hydrolysis of its terminal phosphate drives most cell work.

name: Guanosine monophosphate (GMP)
description: Guanine ribonucleotide with one phosphate; an RNA monomer and a flavor enhancer.

name: Guanosine diphosphate (GDP)
description: Guanine nucleotide with two phosphates; holds G proteins in their inactive state.

name: Guanosine triphosphate (GTP)
description: Guanine nucleotide with three phosphates; fuels protein synthesis and activates G proteins.

name: Uridine monophosphate (UMP)
description: Uracil ribonucleotide; the first pyrimidine nucleotide made in de novo synthesis.

name: Uridine triphosphate (UTP)
description: Uracil nucleotide with three phosphates; an RNA precursor that also activates sugars as UDP-glucose.

name: Cytidine monophosphate (CMP)
description: Cytosine ribonucleotide with one phosphate; an RNA monomer and part of CMP-sialic acid.

name: Cytidine triphosphate (CTP)
description: Cytosine nucleotide with three phosphates; an RNA precursor and activator of phospholipid head groups.

name: Inosine monophosphate (IMP)
description: First purine nucleotide made in de novo synthesis; the branch point to AMP and GMP.

name: Cyclic AMP (cAMP)
description: Second messenger made from ATP by adenylyl cyclase; activates protein kinase A in hormone signaling.

name: Cyclic GMP (cGMP)
description: Second messenger made from GTP; relaxes smooth muscle and carries the light signal in the retina.

name: Deoxyadenosine triphosphate (dATP)
description: Deoxyribonucleotide that DNA polymerase adds opposite thymine during DNA replication.

name: Deoxyguanosine triphosphate (dGTP)
description: Deoxyribonucleotide that DNA polymerase adds opposite cytosine during DNA replication.

name: Deoxycytidine triphosphate (dCTP)
description: Deoxyribonucleotide that DNA polymerase adds opposite guanine during DNA replication.

name: Thymidine triphosphate (dTTP)
description: Deoxyribonucleotide that DNA polymerase adds opposite adenine during DNA replication.

name: NAD+
description: Oxidized dinucleotide coenzyme that accepts hydride in glycolysis and the citric acid cycle.

name: NADH
description: Reduced form of NAD+; carries electrons from catabolism to complex I of the respiratory chain.

name: NADP+
description: Phosphorylated form of NAD+; the electron acceptor of photosynthesis and the pentose phosphate pathway.

name: NADPH
description: Reduced form of NADP+; supplies electrons for fatty acid synthesis and antioxidant defense.

name: Flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD)
description: Riboflavin-derived redox coenzyme bound to enzymes such as succinate dehydrogenase.

name: Flavin mononucleotide (FMN)
description: Riboflavin 5'-phosphate; the redox cofactor of complex I and of many flavoproteins.

name: Orotic acid
description: Pyrimidine precursor made in de novo synthesis; joined to PRPP on the way to UMP.

name: D-Glucose (open chain)
description: Open-chain aldehyde form of glucose; under 1% of glucose in water is in this linear form.

name: alpha-D-Glucopyranose
description: Six-membered ring form of glucose with an axial anomeric OH; the unit of starch and glycogen.

name: beta-D-Glucopyranose
description: Ring form of glucose with every OH equatorial; the main form in solution and the unit of cellulose.

name: D-Fructose (open chain)
description: Open-chain ketone form of fructose, the sweetest common natural sugar, found in fruit and honey.

name: beta-D-Fructofuranose
description: Five-membered ring form of fructose; the form bound in sucrose and in fructose phosphates.

name: beta-D-Fructopyranose
description: Six-membered ring form of fructose; the main form of free fructose in crystals and in water.

name: D-Galactose (open chain)
description: Open-chain form of galactose, the C4 epimer of glucose released from lactose by digestion.

name: alpha-D-Galactopyranose
description: Alpha ring form of galactose; found in raffinose and in blood group B antigens.

name: beta-D-Galactopyranose
description: Beta ring form of galactose; joined to glucose in lactose, the sugar of milk.

name: D-Ribose (open chain)
description: Open-chain form of ribose, the five-carbon aldose sugar of RNA and ATP.

name: beta-D-Ribofuranose
description: Five-membered ring form of ribose; the sugar unit in RNA, ATP, NAD+ and coenzyme A.

name: 2-Deoxy-D-ribose
description: Ribose missing the 2' hydroxyl; the sugar of DNA, which makes DNA more stable than RNA.

name: alpha-D-Mannopyranose
description: Ring form of mannose, the C2 epimer of glucose; a main sugar of glycoprotein glycans.

name: D-Xylose
description: Five-carbon aldose that makes up hemicellulose xylan in wood; the source of xylitol.

name: L-Arabinose
description: Five-carbon aldose in plant cell wall pectin and hemicellulose; used to switch on genes in bacteria.

name: D-Glyceraldehyde
description: Simplest aldose with three carbons; the reference compound for D and L sugar configuration.

name: Dihydroxyacetone
description: Simplest ketose with three carbons; its phosphate is a glycolysis intermediate and it browns skin in sunless tanners.

name: D-Erythrose
description: Four-carbon aldose; its 4-phosphate feeds the shikimate pathway to aromatic amino acids.

name: D-Ribulose
description: Five-carbon ketose; its 1,5-bisphosphate is the CO2 acceptor of RuBisCO in photosynthesis.

name: D-Xylulose
description: Five-carbon ketose; its 5-phosphate is an intermediate of the pentose phosphate pathway.

name: Sedoheptulose
description: Seven-carbon ketose found in plants; its 7-phosphate is a pentose phosphate pathway intermediate.

name: L-Fucose
description: 6-Deoxy-L-galactose found on cell-surface glycans, including the ABO blood group antigens.

name: L-Rhamnose
description: 6-Deoxy-L-mannose found in plant pectin, flavonoid glycosides and bacterial cell walls.

name: D-Tagatose
description: Rare ketohexose, the C4 epimer of fructose, found in small amounts in heated dairy products.

name: D-Psicose (allulose)
description: Rare ketohexose, the C3 epimer of fructose, found in small amounts in wheat and figs.

name: Sucrose
description: Table sugar, glucose and fructose joined by an alpha-1,2 bond; the transport sugar of plants.

name: Lactose
description: Milk sugar, galactose joined to glucose by a beta-1,4 bond; digested by the enzyme lactase.

name: Maltose
description: Two glucose units joined by an alpha-1,4 bond; released when amylase digests starch.

name: Trehalose
description: Two glucose units joined 1,1 at both anomeric carbons; protects insects, yeasts and plants from drying.

name: Cellobiose
description: Two glucose units joined by a beta-1,4 bond; the repeating unit of cellulose.

name: Isomaltose
description: Two glucose units joined by an alpha-1,6 bond, as at the branch points of starch and glycogen.

name: Lactulose
description: Synthetic disaccharide of galactose and fructose; not digested in the small intestine.

name: Raffinose
description: Trisaccharide of galactose, glucose and fructose found in beans and cabbage; fermented by gut bacteria.

name: Stachyose
description: Tetrasaccharide of two galactoses, glucose and fructose; a storage sugar in legume seeds.

name: Sorbitol
description: Sugar alcohol made by reducing glucose; found in fruits such as apples and pears and used as a sweetener.

name: Xylitol
description: Five-carbon sugar alcohol from xylose; a sweetener that oral bacteria cannot ferment.

name: Erythritol
description: Four-carbon sugar alcohol found in fruits and fermented foods; a low-calorie sweetener.

name: Mannitol
description: Sugar alcohol made by reducing mannose; abundant in brown algae, fungi and the manna ash tree.

name: Ribitol
description: Five-carbon sugar alcohol from ribose; forms the side chain of riboflavin and part of teichoic acids.

name: Glycerol
description: Three-carbon triol that forms the backbone of triglycerides and phospholipids.

name: myo-Inositol
description: Cyclic sugar alcohol; the head group of phosphoinositide lipids and of inositol phosphate messengers.

name: D-Glucosamine
description: Amino sugar with NH2 at C2 of glucose; a building block of chitin and glycosaminoglycans.

name: N-Acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc)
description: Acetylated glucosamine; the repeating unit of chitin and part of bacterial peptidoglycan.

name: N-Acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)
description: Acetylated galactosamine; starts O-linked glycans on proteins and is in the blood group A antigen.

name: N-Acetylneuraminic acid (sialic acid)
description: Nine-carbon acidic sugar that caps cell-surface glycans; the receptor for influenza virus.

name: Muramic acid
description: Glucosamine linked to lactic acid; found only in bacterial cell wall peptidoglycan.

name: D-Glucuronic acid
description: Glucose oxidized at C6; liver cells attach glucuronic acid to drugs and bilirubin for excretion.

name: D-Galacturonic acid
description: Galactose oxidized at C6; the main unit of pectin in plant cell walls.

name: D-Gluconic acid
description: Glucose oxidized at C1; found in honey and wine and made by glucose oxidase.

name: alpha-Cyclodextrin
description: Ring of six alpha-1,4 linked glucose units with a hydrophobic cavity that holds small molecules.

name: Butyric acid
description: Four-carbon short-chain fatty acid made by gut bacteria from fiber; a main fuel for colon cells.

name: Caproic acid
description: Six-carbon saturated fatty acid found in goat milk fat and coconut oil; has a strong goat-like odor.

name: Caprylic acid
description: Eight-carbon saturated fatty acid found in coconut oil and milk; a medium-chain triglyceride component.

name: Capric acid
description: Ten-carbon saturated fatty acid found in coconut oil, palm kernel oil and goat milk.

name: Lauric acid
description: Twelve-carbon saturated fatty acid; the main fatty acid of coconut and palm kernel oil.

name: Myristic acid
description: Fourteen-carbon saturated fatty acid in nutmeg and milk fat; attached to proteins to anchor them to membranes.

name: Palmitic acid
description: Sixteen-carbon saturated fatty acid; the first product of fatty acid synthase and the most common fat in animals.

name: Stearic acid
description: Eighteen-carbon saturated fatty acid abundant in animal fat and cocoa butter.

name: Arachidic acid
description: Twenty-carbon saturated fatty acid found in small amounts in peanut oil.

name: Behenic acid
description: Twenty-two-carbon saturated fatty acid found in ben oil from moringa seeds and in rapeseed.

name: Lignoceric acid
description: Twenty-four-carbon saturated fatty acid in wood tar and brain sphingolipids; builds up in adrenoleukodystrophy.

name: Palmitoleic acid
description: Sixteen-carbon omega-7 monounsaturated fatty acid found in macadamia oil and human fat tissue.

name: Oleic acid
description: Eighteen-carbon cis monounsaturated fatty acid; the main fatty acid of olive oil.

name: Elaidic acid
description: Trans isomer of oleic acid; the main trans fat formed in partial hydrogenation of vegetable oils.

name: Vaccenic acid
description: Eighteen-carbon trans omega-7 fatty acid; the main natural trans fat in milk and ruminant fat.

name: Erucic acid
description: Twenty-two-carbon omega-9 monounsaturated fatty acid abundant in traditional rapeseed and mustard oil.

name: Nervonic acid
description: Twenty-four-carbon omega-9 monounsaturated fatty acid enriched in the myelin sphingolipids of nerves.

name: Linoleic acid
description: Essential omega-6 fatty acid with two cis double bonds; abundant in sunflower, corn and soybean oil.

name: gamma-Linolenic acid
description: Omega-6 fatty acid with three double bonds found in evening primrose and borage oil.

name: alpha-Linolenic acid
description: Essential omega-3 fatty acid with three cis double bonds; abundant in flaxseed, chia and walnut oil.

name: Arachidonic acid
description: Omega-6 fatty acid with four double bonds; the precursor of prostaglandins, thromboxanes and leukotrienes.

name: Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA)
description: Omega-3 fatty acid with five double bonds found in oily fish; precursor of anti-inflammatory mediators.

name: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA)
description: Omega-3 fatty acid with six double bonds; a major structural fat of brain and retinal membranes.

name: Phytanic acid
description: Branched-chain fatty acid from chlorophyll's phytol tail; accumulates in Refsum disease.

name: Tripalmitin
description: Triglyceride of three palmitic acids on glycerol; a saturated fat found in palm oil.

name: Tristearin
description: Triglyceride of three stearic acids on glycerol; a solid fat found in beef tallow and cocoa butter.

name: Triolein
description: Triglyceride of three oleic acids on glycerol; a main component of olive oil.

name: DPPC (dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine)
description: Saturated phosphatidylcholine; the main surface-active lipid of lung surfactant.

name: POPC (a phosphatidylcholine)
description: Phosphatidylcholine with palmitic and oleic tails; a typical lipid of eukaryotic cell membranes.

name: POPE (a phosphatidylethanolamine)
description: Phosphatidylethanolamine with a small head group; common in inner membranes and bacterial membranes.

name: POPS (a phosphatidylserine)
description: Phosphatidylserine kept on the inner membrane leaflet; exposed on the surface of dying cells.

name: Sphingosine
description: Eighteen-carbon amino alcohol that forms the backbone of ceramides, sphingomyelin and gangliosides.

name: Sphingosine 1-phosphate
description: Phosphorylated sphingosine; a blood-borne lipid signal that guides immune cell movement.

name: Ceramide (C16)
description: Sphingosine with an amide-linked palmitic acid; a skin barrier lipid and a signal in cell death.

name: Cholesterol
description: Four-ring sterol of animal cell membranes that controls fluidity; precursor of steroid hormones and bile acids.

name: Cholesteryl oleate
description: Cholesterol esterified with oleic acid; the main storage form of cholesterol in LDL particles.

name: 7-Dehydrocholesterol
description: Immediate precursor of cholesterol; ultraviolet light converts it in the skin to vitamin D3.

name: Ergosterol
description: Main sterol of fungal cell membranes; the target of antifungal drugs and precursor of vitamin D2.

name: beta-Sitosterol
description: Most common plant sterol, found in nuts, seeds and vegetable oils; lowers cholesterol uptake from the gut.

name: Stigmasterol
description: Plant sterol with an extra side-chain double bond; found in soybeans and calabar beans.

name: Squalene
description: Thirty-carbon triterpene hydrocarbon; precursor of all sterols and abundant in shark liver oil.

name: Lanosterol
description: First four-ring sterol formed when squalene epoxide cyclizes; precursor of cholesterol in animals and fungi.

name: Prostaglandin E2
description: Arachidonic acid derivative made by COX enzymes; causes fever, pain and inflammation.

name: Prostaglandin F2alpha
description: Prostaglandin that contracts uterine smooth muscle and ends the corpus luteum.

name: Prostacyclin (PGI2)
description: Prostaglandin made by blood vessel walls that dilates vessels and stops platelet aggregation.

name: Thromboxane A2
description: Unstable eicosanoid made by platelets that causes platelet aggregation and vessel constriction.

name: Leukotriene B4
description: Arachidonic acid derivative made by lipoxygenase; attracts neutrophils to sites of inflammation.

name: Cholic acid
description: Primary bile acid made from cholesterol in the liver; emulsifies dietary fat in the gut.

name: Chenodeoxycholic acid
description: Primary bile acid with two hydroxyl groups, made from cholesterol in the liver.

name: Deoxycholic acid
description: Secondary bile acid made when gut bacteria remove the 7-hydroxyl of cholic acid.

name: Glycocholic acid
description: Cholic acid conjugated with glycine in the liver; a main bile salt in human bile.

name: Taurocholic acid
description: Cholic acid conjugated with taurine in the liver; a strong detergent bile salt.

name: Retinol (vitamin A1)
description: All-trans vitamin A alcohol stored in the liver as esters; precursor of retinal and retinoic acid.

name: Retinal
description: All-trans aldehyde form of vitamin A; the form released when rhodopsin absorbs light.

name: 11-cis-Retinal
description: Bent aldehyde of vitamin A bound to opsin in rhodopsin; light flips it to the all-trans form.

name: Retinoic acid
description: Acid form of vitamin A that binds nuclear receptors; guides embryonic development and skin cell growth.

name: beta-Carotene
description: Orange plant pigment in carrots and sweet potato; cleaved in the gut into two molecules of retinal.

name: Thiamine (vitamin B1)
description: Vitamin B1, a thiazolium and pyrimidine compound; deficiency causes beriberi.

name: Thiamine pyrophosphate
description: Active coenzyme form of vitamin B1; used by pyruvate dehydrogenase and transketolase.

name: Riboflavin (vitamin B2)
description: Vitamin B2, a yellow isoalloxazine; the precursor of the redox coenzymes FMN and FAD.

name: Niacin (vitamin B3)
description: Vitamin B3 acid form; precursor of NAD+ and NADP+, and deficiency causes pellagra.

name: Nicotinamide
description: Amide form of vitamin B3; the redox-active part of NAD+ and NADP+.

name: Pantothenic acid (vitamin B5)
description: Vitamin B5, made of pantoic acid and beta-alanine; the precursor of coenzyme A.

name: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6)
description: Alcohol form of vitamin B6 found in plant foods; converted in the body to pyridoxal phosphate.

name: Pyridoxal
description: Aldehyde form of vitamin B6; phosphorylated to make the active coenzyme.

name: Pyridoxamine
description: Amine form of vitamin B6; carries the amino group during transamination.

name: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate
description: Active coenzyme of vitamin B6; used by transaminases and decarboxylases in amino acid metabolism.

name: Biotin (vitamin B7)
description: Vitamin B7, a sulfur-containing ring compound; the CO2 carrier for carboxylase enzymes.

name: Folic acid (vitamin B9)
description: Synthetic oxidized vitamin B9; reduced in the body to tetrahydrofolate, which carries one-carbon units.

name: L-Methylfolate
description: 5-Methyltetrahydrofolate, the main form of folate in blood; donates a methyl group to homocysteine.

name: Cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12)
description: Vitamin B12 with a cyanide ligand on cobalt; the stable form used in supplements.

name: Methylcobalamin
description: Coenzyme form of vitamin B12 used by methionine synthase to recycle homocysteine.

name: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C)
description: Vitamin C, a reducing sugar acid; needed to hydroxylate collagen, and deficiency causes scurvy.

name: Dehydroascorbic acid
description: Oxidized form of vitamin C; taken up by cells through glucose transporters and reduced back.

name: Ergocalciferol (vitamin D2)
description: Vitamin D2 made when ultraviolet light strikes ergosterol in fungi and yeast.

name: Cholecalciferol (vitamin D3)
description: Vitamin D3 made in skin from 7-dehydrocholesterol by ultraviolet B light.

name: Calcifediol
description: 25-Hydroxyvitamin D3, made in the liver; the main circulating form measured to assess vitamin D status.

name: Calcitriol
description: 1,25-Dihydroxyvitamin D3, the active hormone made in the kidney; raises calcium uptake from the gut.

name: alpha-Tocopherol (vitamin E)
description: Main form of vitamin E; a lipid-soluble antioxidant that protects membranes from peroxidation.

name: gamma-Tocopherol
description: Form of vitamin E most common in the American diet, found in soybean and corn oil.

name: Phylloquinone (vitamin K1)
description: Vitamin K1 from green plants; needed to carboxylate blood clotting factors.

name: Menaquinone-4 (vitamin K2)
description: Vitamin K2 form with four isoprene units, made in animal tissues from other K vitamins.

name: Menadione (vitamin K3)
description: Synthetic naphthoquinone with no side chain; converted in the body to menaquinone-4.

name: Choline
description: Quaternary ammonium nutrient; part of phosphatidylcholine and the precursor of acetylcholine.

name: Glucose 6-phosphate
description: First product of glycolysis, made by hexokinase; the branch point to glycogen and the pentose phosphate pathway.

name: Fructose 6-phosphate
description: Glycolysis intermediate made by isomerizing glucose 6-phosphate; substrate of phosphofructokinase.

name: Fructose 1,6-bisphosphate
description: Product of phosphofructokinase, the committed step of glycolysis; split by aldolase into two trioses.

name: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate
description: Triose phosphate from aldolase; isomerized to glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate or reduced to glycerol phosphate.

name: Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
description: Triose phosphate oxidized in glycolysis to make NADH; also a product of the Calvin cycle.

name: 1,3-Bisphosphoglycerate
description: High-energy acyl phosphate in glycolysis; gives a phosphate to ADP to make the first ATP.

name: 3-Phosphoglycerate
description: Glycolysis intermediate and the first stable product of carbon fixation by RuBisCO.

name: 2-Phosphoglycerate
description: Glycolysis intermediate dehydrated by enolase to phosphoenolpyruvate.

name: Phosphoenolpyruvate
description: Highest-energy phosphate in glycolysis; pyruvate kinase transfers its phosphate to ADP.

name: Pyruvic acid
description: End product of glycolysis; converted to acetyl-CoA, lactate, alanine or oxaloacetate.

name: L-Lactic acid
description: Product of anaerobic glycolysis in muscle; recycled to glucose by the liver in the Cori cycle.

name: Acetyl-CoA
description: Acetyl group bound to coenzyme A; feeds the citric acid cycle and fatty acid and sterol synthesis.

name: Coenzyme A
description: Pantothenic acid-derived thiol coenzyme that carries acyl groups as thioesters.

name: Malonyl-CoA
description: Carboxylated acetyl-CoA; the two-carbon donor in fatty acid synthesis and a block on fat oxidation.

name: Citric acid
description: Tricarboxylic acid formed from acetyl-CoA and oxaloacetate; the first step of the citric acid cycle.

name: cis-Aconitic acid
description: Citric acid cycle intermediate between citrate and isocitrate, bound to the enzyme aconitase.

name: Isocitric acid
description: Citric acid cycle intermediate oxidized by isocitrate dehydrogenase to release CO2 and NADH.

name: alpha-Ketoglutaric acid
description: Citric acid cycle intermediate that links to amino acid metabolism through glutamate.

name: Succinyl-CoA
description: Citric acid cycle thioester whose cleavage makes GTP; also the starting point of heme synthesis.

name: Succinic acid
description: Citric acid cycle intermediate oxidized to fumarate by complex II of the respiratory chain.

name: Fumaric acid
description: Trans dicarboxylic acid of the citric acid cycle; also made in the urea cycle.

name: L-Malic acid
description: Citric acid cycle intermediate; gives apples their sour taste and shuttles NADH into mitochondria.

name: Oxaloacetic acid
description: Four-carbon keto acid that accepts acetyl-CoA to start the citric acid cycle; a gluconeogenesis precursor.

name: Glyoxylic acid
description: Two-carbon aldehyde acid of the glyoxylate cycle, which lets plants and bacteria make sugar from fat.

name: Ribose 5-phosphate
description: Pentose phosphate pathway product used to make nucleotides and histidine.

name: 6-Phosphogluconic acid
description: Oxidative pentose phosphate pathway intermediate decarboxylated to ribulose 5-phosphate and NADPH.

name: PRPP
description: Activated ribose donor for purine, pyrimidine, histidine and NAD+ synthesis.

name: Acetoacetic acid
description: Ketone body made by the liver from fatty acids during fasting; used as fuel by heart and brain.

name: beta-Hydroxybutyric acid
description: Most abundant ketone body in blood during fasting; the reduced form of acetoacetate.

name: Mevalonic acid
description: Product of HMG-CoA reductase, the target of statins; the precursor of all isoprenoids in animals.

name: Isopentenyl pyrophosphate
description: Five-carbon isoprene unit from which cholesterol, carotenoids and rubber are built.

name: Geranyl pyrophosphate
description: Ten-carbon isoprenoid; the precursor of monoterpenes such as limonene and menthol.

name: Farnesyl pyrophosphate
description: Fifteen-carbon isoprenoid; precursor of squalene and the lipid anchor added to Ras proteins.

name: Carbamoyl phosphate
description: Activated nitrogen donor that starts the urea cycle and pyrimidine synthesis.

name: Argininosuccinic acid
description: Urea cycle intermediate formed from citrulline and aspartate; split into arginine and fumarate.

name: Urea
description: Main nitrogen waste product of mammals, made in the liver urea cycle and excreted in urine.

name: Uric acid
description: End product of purine breakdown in humans and birds; its crystals cause gout.

name: Allantoin
description: Product of uric acid oxidation in most mammals other than humans and great apes.

name: 5-Aminolevulinic acid
description: First committed precursor of heme and chlorophyll, made from glycine and succinyl-CoA in animals.

name: Porphobilinogen
description: Pyrrole made from two 5-aminolevulinic acids; four of them join to form the porphyrin ring.

name: Protoporphyrin IX
description: Porphyrin ring that receives iron to form heme; it accumulates in some porphyrias.

name: Heme b
description: Iron protoporphyrin IX; the oxygen-binding group of hemoglobin and myoglobin and a cytochrome cofactor.

name: Chlorophyll a
description: Magnesium chlorin pigment of all oxygen-producing photosynthesis; absorbs red and blue light.

name: Biliverdin
description: Green linear tetrapyrrole made when heme oxygenase opens the heme ring; colors bruises green.

name: Bilirubin
description: Yellow-orange breakdown product of heme made from biliverdin; builds up in jaundice.

name: Coenzyme Q10 (ubiquinone)
description: Lipid-soluble quinone with ten isoprene units; carries electrons from complexes I and II to complex III.

name: Ubiquinol
description: Reduced form of coenzyme Q10; the electron carrier in membranes and a lipid antioxidant.

name: S-Adenosylmethionine
description: Universal methyl donor made from methionine and ATP; methylates DNA, proteins and small molecules.

name: S-Adenosylhomocysteine
description: Product left after S-adenosylmethionine donates its methyl group; hydrolyzed to homocysteine.

name: Glutathione
description: Tripeptide of glutamate, cysteine and glycine; the main thiol antioxidant inside cells.

name: Glutathione disulfide
description: Oxidized glutathione dimer; reduced back to glutathione by glutathione reductase with NADPH.

name: Phosphocreatine
description: Phosphorylated creatine that buffers ATP in muscle and brain during short bursts of activity.

name: Lipoic acid
description: Dithiolane fatty acid cofactor of pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase.

name: Tetrahydrofolate
description: Reduced folate coenzyme that carries one-carbon units for purine, thymidine and methionine synthesis.

name: Dopaquinone
description: Quinone made by tyrosinase from tyrosine and L-DOPA; the branch point to eumelanin and pheomelanin.

name: 5,6-Dihydroxyindole
description: Indole formed from dopachrome; polymerizes to form the black-brown pigment eumelanin.

name: Testosterone
description: Principal male sex hormone, an androgen made mainly in the testes; isolated and synthesized in 1935.

name: Estradiol
description: The most potent natural estrogen, made mainly in the ovaries; drives female sexual development and cycles.

name: Estrone
description: Weaker estrogen and the main one after menopause; the first steroid hormone isolated, in 1929.

name: Estriol
description: Estrogen produced in large amounts by the placenta during pregnancy; weaker than estradiol.

name: Progesterone
description: Steroid hormone of the menstrual cycle and pregnancy that prepares and maintains the uterine lining.

name: Cortisol
description: Main glucocorticoid stress hormone from the adrenal cortex; raises blood glucose and damps inflammation.

name: Cortisone
description: Inactive glucocorticoid converted to cortisol in tissues; its 1948 use in arthritis won a Nobel Prize.

name: Corticosterone
description: Adrenal glucocorticoid that is the main stress hormone in rodents, birds and reptiles.

name: Aldosterone
description: Mineralocorticoid from the adrenal cortex that makes the kidneys retain sodium and excrete potassium.

name: DHEA
description: Dehydroepiandrosterone, an abundant adrenal steroid that serves as a precursor to androgens and estrogens.

name: Dihydrotestosterone
description: Potent androgen formed from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase; drives prostate growth and male hair patterns.

name: Androstenedione
description: Steroid intermediate made in the adrenals and gonads, converted to testosterone or estrone.

name: Pregnenolone
description: First steroid made from cholesterol in the steroid pathway; the precursor of all other steroid hormones.

name: 17-Hydroxyprogesterone
description: Steroid intermediate on the path to cortisol; measured in newborn screening for adrenal hyperplasia.

name: Allopregnanolone
description: Neurosteroid made from progesterone that enhances GABA-A receptor signaling in the brain.

name: Thyroxine
description: T4, the main hormone secreted by the thyroid gland; an iodinated tyrosine derivative that sets metabolic rate.

name: Triiodothyronine
description: T3, the active thyroid hormone formed from thyroxine; binds nuclear receptors to regulate metabolism.

name: Melatonin
description: Hormone of the pineal gland released in darkness; signals night and helps regulate the sleep-wake cycle.

name: Adrenaline
description: Epinephrine, the fight-or-flight hormone of the adrenal medulla; raises heart rate and blood glucose.

name: Noradrenaline
description: Norepinephrine, the main neurotransmitter of the sympathetic nervous system and a brain arousal signal.

name: Dopamine
description: Catecholamine neurotransmitter for movement, motivation and reward; its loss underlies Parkinson's disease.

name: Serotonin
description: 5-hydroxytryptamine, a neurotransmitter for mood, sleep and gut motility; most of it is made in the gut.

name: Histamine
description: Amine released by mast cells in allergy and inflammation; also a neurotransmitter and stomach acid signal.

name: Acetylcholine
description: First neurotransmitter identified (1921); signals at nerve-muscle junctions and in the autonomic system.

name: GABA
description: Gamma-aminobutyric acid, the main inhibitory neurotransmitter of the mammalian brain.

name: L-DOPA
description: Amino acid precursor of dopamine; given as levodopa, it is the main treatment for Parkinson's disease.

name: Anandamide
description: First endocannabinoid found (1992); a fatty acid amide that activates the brain's cannabinoid receptors.

name: 2-Arachidonoylglycerol
description: 2-AG, the most abundant endocannabinoid; a glycerol ester that acts as a retrograde synaptic signal.

name: Oxytocin
description: Nine-residue peptide hormone for labor contractions and milk let-down; the first peptide hormone synthesized.

name: Vasopressin
description: Antidiuretic hormone, a nine-residue peptide that makes the kidneys conserve water and constricts vessels.

name: Thyrotropin-releasing hormone
description: TRH, a three-residue hypothalamic peptide that triggers release of thyroid-stimulating hormone.

name: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone
description: GnRH, a ten-residue hypothalamic peptide that controls the release of LH and FSH from the pituitary.

name: Angiotensin II
description: Eight-residue peptide of the renin-angiotensin system that constricts vessels and raises blood pressure.

name: Bradykinin
description: Nine-residue peptide that dilates blood vessels and causes pain in inflammation; broken down by ACE.

name: Met-enkephalin
description: Five-residue endogenous opioid peptide, isolated from pig brain in 1975 with Leu-enkephalin.

name: Leu-enkephalin
description: Five-residue endogenous opioid peptide ending in leucine; one of the first natural opioids found.

name: Prostaglandin E2
description: Lipid mediator made by COX enzymes; causes fever, pain and inflammation and ripens the cervix in labor.

name: Prostaglandin F2-alpha
description: Prostaglandin that contracts uterine smooth muscle and ends the corpus luteum in many mammals.

name: Prostacyclin
description: Prostaglandin I2, an eicosanoid made by vessel walls that dilates vessels and inhibits platelets.

name: Indole-3-acetic acid
description: Auxin, the main plant growth hormone; controls cell elongation and bending of shoots toward light.

name: Gibberellic acid
description: Plant hormone first found in a rice fungus; stimulates stem growth and seed germination.

name: Abscisic acid
description: Plant stress hormone that closes stomata during drought and keeps seeds dormant.

name: Zeatin
description: Natural cytokinin first isolated from maize kernels; promotes plant cell division and delays leaf aging.

name: Kinetin
description: First cytokinin discovered (1955), in autoclaved DNA; promotes cell division in plant tissue culture.

name: Jasmonic acid
description: Plant hormone made from linolenic acid that triggers defenses against insects and wounding.

name: Brassinolide
description: Plant steroid hormone first isolated from rapeseed pollen; promotes cell expansion and growth.

name: Strigol
description: First strigolactone found, from cotton roots; signals branching and triggers parasitic weed germination.

name: Juvenile hormone III
description: Insect sesquiterpenoid hormone that keeps larvae in the juvenile state and blocks metamorphosis.

name: Ecdysone
description: Insect steroid molting hormone, isolated from silkworm pupae in 1954; converted to 20-hydroxyecdysone.

name: 20-Hydroxyecdysone
description: Active form of the insect molting hormone; binds the ecdysone receptor to start each molt.

name: Bombykol
description: Sex pheromone of the female silk moth; the first pheromone chemically identified, in 1959.

name: Disparlure
description: Epoxide sex pheromone of the female gypsy moth, used in traps to monitor this forest pest.

name: 9-Oxo-2-decenoic acid
description: Main queen mandibular pheromone of the honeybee; suppresses worker ovaries and attracts drones.

name: Tyramine
description: Trace amine formed from tyrosine and found in aged cheese; releases noradrenaline from nerve endings.

name: Octopamine
description: Invertebrate counterpart of noradrenaline; first found in octopus salivary glands.

name: Tryptamine
description: Trace amine made from tryptophan; the core structure of serotonin, melatonin and many alkaloids.

name: Phenethylamine
description: Trace amine made from phenylalanine; the parent structure of the catecholamines and amphetamines.

name: N-Acetylserotonin
description: Intermediate between serotonin and melatonin in the pineal gland; also active at TrkB receptors.

name: Aspirin
description: Acetylsalicylic acid, an NSAID for pain, fever and clot prevention; marketed by Bayer in 1899.

name: Paracetamol
description: Acetaminophen, a common analgesic and fever reducer with weak anti-inflammatory action; brand Tylenol.

name: Ibuprofen
description: Propionic acid NSAID for pain, fever and inflammation; developed by Boots in the 1960s.

name: Naproxen
description: Long-acting NSAID used for arthritis, menstrual pain and other inflammatory pain.

name: Diclofenac
description: NSAID used for arthritis and acute pain, taken orally or applied as a topical gel.

name: Celecoxib
description: Selective COX-2 inhibitor NSAID for arthritis, designed to reduce stomach side effects; brand Celebrex.

name: Indomethacin
description: Potent NSAID used for gout attacks and arthritis, and to close a patent ductus arteriosus in infants.

name: Ketorolac
description: NSAID for short-term treatment of moderate to severe pain, often given by injection.

name: Meloxicam
description: Oxicam NSAID with partial COX-2 preference, used for osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.

name: Morphine
description: Principal alkaloid of opium, isolated in 1804; an opioid analgesic for severe pain.

name: Codeine
description: Opium alkaloid used for mild pain and cough; converted in the liver to morphine.

name: Oxycodone
description: Semi-synthetic opioid made from thebaine, used for moderate to severe pain.

name: Hydromorphone
description: Semi-synthetic opioid derived from morphine, used for severe pain in hospitals and palliative care.

name: Fentanyl
description: Synthetic opioid anesthetic and analgesic, about 100 times more potent than morphine; made in 1960.

name: Methadone
description: Long-acting synthetic opioid used for chronic pain and for opioid use disorder maintenance.

name: Buprenorphine
description: Partial opioid agonist from thebaine, used for pain and to treat opioid use disorder.

name: Naloxone
description: Opioid receptor antagonist that rapidly reverses opioid overdose; brand Narcan.

name: Naltrexone
description: Long-acting opioid antagonist used to treat alcohol and opioid use disorders.

name: Tramadol
description: Weak opioid analgesic that also blocks serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake; used for moderate pain.

name: Penicillin G
description: Benzylpenicillin, the first penicillin used clinically (1940s), from Fleming's 1928 mold discovery.

name: Amoxicillin
description: Broad-spectrum aminopenicillin antibiotic for ear, throat, chest and urinary infections.

name: Ampicillin
description: Early broad-spectrum aminopenicillin antibiotic (1961) active against many gram-negative bacteria.

name: Cephalexin
description: First-generation cephalosporin antibiotic taken orally for skin, bone and urinary infections.

name: Ceftriaxone
description: Third-generation cephalosporin given by injection for meningitis, gonorrhea and severe infections.

name: Meropenem
description: Carbapenem beta-lactam antibiotic with a very broad spectrum, reserved for serious hospital infections.

name: Ciprofloxacin
description: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic that blocks bacterial DNA gyrase; used for urinary and gut infections.

name: Levofloxacin
description: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic, the active L-isomer of ofloxacin, used for pneumonia and sinus infections.

name: Doxycycline
description: Tetracycline antibiotic for acne, Lyme disease, chlamydia and malaria prevention.

name: Tetracycline
description: Broad-spectrum antibiotic from Streptomyces that blocks the bacterial ribosome; introduced in the 1950s.

name: Azithromycin
description: Macrolide antibiotic with a long half-life, used for respiratory and sexually transmitted infections.

name: Erythromycin
description: Macrolide antibiotic from Saccharopolyspora erythraea (1952), an option for penicillin allergy.

name: Clarithromycin
description: Macrolide antibiotic used for respiratory infections and in Helicobacter pylori treatment.

name: Vancomycin
description: Glycopeptide antibiotic that blocks cell wall building; a key treatment for MRSA infections.

name: Sulfamethoxazole
description: Sulfonamide antibiotic that blocks bacterial folate synthesis; usually paired with trimethoprim.

name: Trimethoprim
description: Antibiotic that inhibits bacterial dihydrofolate reductase; used for urinary tract infections.

name: Metronidazole
description: Nitroimidazole that kills anaerobic bacteria and protozoa such as Giardia and Trichomonas.

name: Chloramphenicol
description: Broad-spectrum antibiotic from Streptomyces (1947); now limited by its rare bone marrow toxicity.

name: Linezolid
description: Oxazolidinone antibiotic that blocks bacterial protein synthesis; used for resistant gram-positive infections.

name: Clindamycin
description: Lincosamide antibiotic for skin, bone and anaerobic infections, also used topically for acne.

name: Gentamicin
description: Aminoglycoside antibiotic from Micromonospora, given by injection for serious gram-negative infections.

name: Nitrofurantoin
description: Antibiotic that concentrates in urine, used to treat and prevent bladder infections.

name: Rifampicin
description: Rifamycin antibiotic that blocks bacterial RNA polymerase; a first-line drug for tuberculosis.

name: Isoniazid
description: First-line tuberculosis drug since 1952 that blocks mycolic acid synthesis in mycobacteria.

name: Ethambutol
description: First-line tuberculosis drug that blocks building of the mycobacterial cell wall.

name: Pyrazinamide
description: First-line tuberculosis drug that shortens therapy by killing slow-growing bacilli.

name: Acyclovir
description: Guanosine analog antiviral for herpes simplex and shingles; its discovery led to a 1988 Nobel Prize.

name: Valacyclovir
description: Valine ester prodrug of acyclovir with better oral uptake, used for herpes and shingles.

name: Oseltamivir
description: Neuraminidase inhibitor antiviral for influenza A and B; brand Tamiflu.

name: Zidovudine
description: AZT, the first approved HIV drug (1987); a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor.

name: Lamivudine
description: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used in HIV combination therapy and for hepatitis B.

name: Tenofovir
description: Nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor for HIV and hepatitis B, given as prodrug salts.

name: Efavirenz
description: Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor long used in first-line HIV combination therapy.

name: Dolutegravir
description: HIV integrase inhibitor that blocks insertion of viral DNA into the host genome.

name: Ritonavir
description: HIV protease inhibitor now used mainly at low doses to boost levels of other antivirals.

name: Remdesivir
description: Nucleotide prodrug that blocks viral RNA polymerase; approved for COVID-19 in 2020.

name: Nirmatrelvir
description: SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitor taken with ritonavir for COVID-19; brand Paxlovid.

name: Sofosbuvir
description: Nucleotide inhibitor of the hepatitis C NS5B polymerase; part of curative hepatitis C regimens.

name: Fluconazole
description: Triazole antifungal for candida infections and cryptococcal meningitis.

name: Ketoconazole
description: Imidazole antifungal now used mainly in creams and shampoos for skin and scalp infections.

name: Clotrimazole
description: Imidazole antifungal applied to the skin for athlete's foot, ringworm and yeast infections.

name: Terbinafine
description: Allylamine antifungal that blocks squalene epoxidase; used for nail and skin fungal infections.

name: Amphotericin B
description: Polyene antifungal from Streptomyces that binds ergosterol; used for severe systemic fungal infections.

name: Nystatin
description: Polyene antifungal discovered in 1950 by two New York State researchers; used for oral and skin candida.

name: Griseofulvin
description: Antifungal from Penicillium molds, taken orally for ringworm of the scalp, skin and nails.

name: Ivermectin B1a
description: Major component of ivermectin, an antiparasitic for river blindness; its discovery won a 2015 Nobel Prize.

name: Praziquantel
description: Anthelmintic used for schistosomiasis and tapeworm infections.

name: Albendazole
description: Benzimidazole anthelmintic that blocks worm tubulin; used for many intestinal worm infections.

name: Mefloquine
description: Quinoline antimalarial used for treatment and prevention of malaria.

name: Chloroquine
description: Synthetic 4-aminoquinoline antimalarial widely used from the 1940s; resistance is now common.

name: Hydroxychloroquine
description: Antimalarial derivative of chloroquine, now mainly used for lupus and rheumatoid arthritis.

name: Atorvastatin
description: Statin that inhibits HMG-CoA reductase to lower LDL cholesterol; brand Lipitor.

name: Simvastatin
description: Statin made from a fungal product (lovastatin) that lowers LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular risk.

name: Rosuvastatin
description: High-potency synthetic statin that lowers LDL cholesterol; brand Crestor.

name: Ezetimibe
description: Cholesterol absorption inhibitor that blocks the NPC1L1 transporter in the gut.

name: Lisinopril
description: ACE inhibitor for high blood pressure and heart failure; a lysine analog of enalaprilat.

name: Enalapril
description: ACE inhibitor prodrug for hypertension and heart failure, converted to enalaprilat in the liver.

name: Ramipril
description: ACE inhibitor used for hypertension and to reduce cardiovascular risk after heart attack.

name: Losartan
description: First angiotensin II receptor blocker (1995), used for high blood pressure and kidney protection.

name: Valsartan
description: Angiotensin II receptor blocker for hypertension and heart failure.

name: Amlodipine
description: Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker for high blood pressure and angina.

name: Nifedipine
description: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that relaxes arteries; used for hypertension and angina.

name: Diltiazem
description: Benzothiazepine calcium channel blocker for angina, hypertension and atrial fibrillation rate control.

name: Verapamil
description: Phenylalkylamine calcium channel blocker that slows heart conduction; used for arrhythmias and angina.

name: Metoprolol
description: Beta-1 selective beta blocker for hypertension, angina, heart failure and after heart attacks.

name: Propranolol
description: First successful beta blocker (1960s), whose developer James Black won a Nobel Prize.

name: Atenolol
description: Water-soluble beta-1 selective beta blocker used for high blood pressure and angina.

name: Carvedilol
description: Beta blocker that also blocks alpha-1 receptors; used for heart failure and hypertension.

name: Warfarin
description: Vitamin K antagonist anticoagulant first sold as a rat poison in 1948; brand Coumadin.

name: Apixaban
description: Direct factor Xa inhibitor anticoagulant for atrial fibrillation and venous clots; brand Eliquis.

name: Rivaroxaban
description: Oral direct factor Xa inhibitor anticoagulant for stroke prevention and deep vein thrombosis.

name: Clopidogrel
description: Antiplatelet prodrug that blocks the P2Y12 ADP receptor; used after heart attacks and stents.

name: Digoxin
description: Cardiac glycoside from the foxglove Digitalis lanata; used for heart failure and atrial fibrillation.

name: Amiodarone
description: Iodine-rich antiarrhythmic drug used for serious ventricular and atrial rhythm disorders.

name: Furosemide
description: Loop diuretic that blocks salt uptake in the kidney; used for edema and heart failure.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
description: Thiazide diuretic used for high blood pressure and fluid retention.

name: Spironolactone
description: Steroid aldosterone antagonist and potassium-sparing diuretic for heart failure and hypertension.

name: Hydralazine
description: Direct arterial vasodilator used for hypertension, including high blood pressure in pregnancy.

name: Clonidine
description: Alpha-2 adrenergic agonist that lowers sympathetic tone; used for hypertension and ADHD.

name: Metformin
description: Biguanide that lowers liver glucose output; first-line drug for type 2 diabetes, from French lilac lore.

name: Glipizide
description: Sulfonylurea that stimulates insulin release from the pancreas in type 2 diabetes.

name: Glibenclamide
description: Glyburide, a second-generation sulfonylurea that stimulates insulin release in type 2 diabetes.

name: Pioglitazone
description: Thiazolidinedione that activates PPAR-gamma to improve insulin sensitivity in type 2 diabetes.

name: Sitagliptin
description: DPP-4 inhibitor that prolongs incretin hormone action in type 2 diabetes; brand Januvia.

name: Empagliflozin
description: SGLT2 inhibitor that makes the kidneys excrete glucose; used in diabetes and heart failure.

name: Dapagliflozin
description: SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes, heart failure and chronic kidney disease.

name: Fluoxetine
description: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor antidepressant, approved in 1987; brand Prozac.

name: Sertraline
description: SSRI antidepressant used for depression, panic disorder, OCD and PTSD; brand Zoloft.

name: Citalopram
description: Racemic SSRI antidepressant used for depression; the parent of escitalopram.

name: Escitalopram
description: S-enantiomer of citalopram, an SSRI for depression and generalized anxiety disorder.

name: Paroxetine
description: SSRI antidepressant used for depression, panic disorder and social anxiety.

name: Venlafaxine
description: Serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (SNRI) antidepressant for depression and anxiety.

name: Duloxetine
description: SNRI used for depression, anxiety, diabetic nerve pain and fibromyalgia.

name: Bupropion
description: Antidepressant that inhibits dopamine and noradrenaline reuptake; also used for smoking cessation.

name: Mirtazapine
description: Tetracyclic antidepressant that blocks alpha-2 receptors; often used when sleep is poor.

name: Trazodone
description: Serotonin antagonist and reuptake inhibitor antidepressant, often prescribed for insomnia.

name: Amitriptyline
description: Tricyclic antidepressant now widely used at low doses for nerve pain and migraine prevention.

name: Imipramine
description: First tricyclic antidepressant, found in 1957 during a search for antipsychotics.

name: Diazepam
description: Benzodiazepine for anxiety, muscle spasm, alcohol withdrawal and seizures; brand Valium (1963).

name: Alprazolam
description: Triazolobenzodiazepine used for anxiety and panic disorder; brand Xanax.

name: Lorazepam
description: Benzodiazepine used for anxiety, sedation before procedures and prolonged seizures.

name: Midazolam
description: Short-acting water-soluble benzodiazepine used for sedation and before anesthesia.

name: Zolpidem
description: Non-benzodiazepine hypnotic that acts at GABA-A receptors; used short-term for insomnia.

name: Buspirone
description: Anxiolytic that acts as a serotonin 5-HT1A partial agonist; not a benzodiazepine.

name: Haloperidol
description: Butyrophenone typical antipsychotic (1958) that blocks dopamine D2 receptors.

name: Chlorpromazine
description: First antipsychotic drug (1952), a phenothiazine that transformed psychiatric care.

name: Clozapine
description: Atypical antipsychotic reserved for treatment-resistant schizophrenia; needs blood count monitoring.

name: Risperidone
description: Atypical antipsychotic for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder that blocks D2 and 5-HT2A receptors.

name: Olanzapine
description: Atypical antipsychotic of the thienobenzodiazepine class for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

name: Quetiapine
description: Atypical antipsychotic used for schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and as add-on for depression.

name: Aripiprazole
description: Atypical antipsychotic that is a dopamine D2 partial agonist; used for schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.

name: Methylphenidate
description: Central nervous system stimulant that blocks dopamine reuptake; an ADHD medicine, brand Ritalin.

name: Amphetamine
description: Central nervous system stimulant used as an ADHD and narcolepsy medicine; first made in 1887.

name: Atomoxetine
description: Non-stimulant ADHD medicine that selectively inhibits noradrenaline reuptake.

name: Modafinil
description: Wakefulness-promoting agent used for narcolepsy and shift work sleep disorder.

name: Carbamazepine
description: Anticonvulsant that blocks sodium channels; used for epilepsy, trigeminal neuralgia and bipolar disorder.

name: Valproic acid
description: Branched fatty acid anticonvulsant for epilepsy and bipolar disorder; its activity was found by chance in 1962.

name: Lamotrigine
description: Anticonvulsant that blocks sodium channels; used for epilepsy and bipolar depression.

name: Levetiracetam
description: Anticonvulsant that binds synaptic vesicle protein SV2A; widely used for epilepsy.

name: Phenytoin
description: Hydantoin anticonvulsant introduced in 1938; blocks sodium channels to control seizures.

name: Phenobarbital
description: Barbiturate anticonvulsant in use since 1912; still common for epilepsy in many countries.

name: Topiramate
description: Sugar-derived anticonvulsant used for epilepsy and migraine prevention.

name: Gabapentin
description: GABA analog that binds the alpha-2-delta calcium channel subunit; used for seizures and nerve pain.

name: Pregabalin
description: Alpha-2-delta ligand related to gabapentin, used for nerve pain, fibromyalgia and anxiety.

name: Donepezil
description: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that eases symptoms of Alzheimer's disease; brand Aricept.

name: Memantine
description: NMDA receptor antagonist used for moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease.

name: Sumatriptan
description: First triptan (1991), a serotonin 5-HT1B/1D agonist that treats acute migraine attacks.

name: Ketamine
description: Dissociative anesthetic that blocks NMDA receptors; used in surgery and for treatment-resistant depression.

name: Propofol
description: Short-acting intravenous anesthetic for inducing and maintaining general anesthesia.

name: Lidocaine
description: Amide local anesthetic (1943) that blocks nerve sodium channels; also an antiarrhythmic.

name: Procaine
description: Ester local anesthetic made in 1905 as a safer substitute for cocaine; brand Novocain.

name: Benzocaine
description: Ester local anesthetic applied to skin and mucosa, for example in throat lozenges and gels.

name: Baclofen
description: GABA-B receptor agonist used to relieve muscle spasticity in multiple sclerosis and spinal injury.

name: Varenicline
description: Nicotinic receptor partial agonist derived from cytisine, used to help people quit smoking.

name: Disulfiram
description: Aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor used to deter alcohol use by causing unpleasant reactions.

name: Omeprazole
description: First proton pump inhibitor (1989) that reduces stomach acid for ulcers and reflux; brand Prilosec.

name: Esomeprazole
description: S-enantiomer of omeprazole, a proton pump inhibitor for reflux and ulcers; brand Nexium.

name: Ranitidine
description: H2 receptor antagonist for ulcers and reflux; withdrawn in 2020 over an NDMA impurity.

name: Famotidine
description: H2 receptor antagonist that reduces stomach acid; used for heartburn and ulcers.

name: Loperamide
description: Opioid receptor agonist that acts on the gut wall to treat diarrhea; brand Imodium.

name: Ondansetron
description: Serotonin 5-HT3 antagonist that prevents nausea from chemotherapy and surgery.

name: Metoclopramide
description: Dopamine antagonist that speeds stomach emptying and relieves nausea.

name: Loratadine
description: Non-sedating H1 antihistamine for hay fever and hives; brand Claritin.

name: Cetirizine
description: Second-generation H1 antihistamine for allergies and hives; a metabolite of hydroxyzine.

name: Fexofenadine
description: Non-sedating H1 antihistamine, the active metabolite of terfenadine; brand Allegra.

name: Diphenhydramine
description: First-generation sedating H1 antihistamine (1946) for allergies and short-term sleep aid.

name: Salbutamol
description: Albuterol, a short-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler that relieves asthma bronchospasm.

name: Montelukast
description: Leukotriene receptor antagonist taken orally for asthma and allergic rhinitis.

name: Pseudoephedrine
description: Sympathomimetic nasal decongestant, a stereoisomer of ephedrine; brand Sudafed.

name: Budesonide
description: Inhaled and oral corticosteroid used for asthma, COPD and inflammatory bowel disease.

name: Fluticasone propionate
description: Inhaled and nasal corticosteroid for asthma and allergic rhinitis; brand Flonase.

name: Ipratropium
description: Inhaled anticholinergic bronchodilator for COPD, derived from atropine.

name: Prednisone
description: Synthetic glucocorticoid prodrug converted to prednisolone; used for many inflammatory diseases.

name: Prednisolone
description: Synthetic glucocorticoid used for asthma, autoimmune disease and inflammation.

name: Dexamethasone
description: Potent long-acting fluorinated glucocorticoid for inflammation, brain swelling and severe COVID-19.

name: Paclitaxel
description: Taxane from the Pacific yew that stabilizes microtubules; used for ovarian, breast and lung cancer.

name: Doxorubicin
description: Anthracycline anticancer antibiotic from Streptomyces that intercalates DNA; used for many cancers.

name: Methotrexate
description: Folate antagonist used for leukemia and other cancers and, at low doses, rheumatoid arthritis.

name: Imatinib
description: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitor that transformed chronic myeloid leukemia care; brand Gleevec.

name: Tamoxifen
description: Selective estrogen receptor modulator used to treat and prevent estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer.

name: Fluorouracil
description: 5-FU, a pyrimidine analog that blocks thymidylate synthase; used for colorectal and other cancers.

name: Cyclophosphamide
description: Alkylating anticancer prodrug activated in the liver; also used as an immunosuppressant.

name: Vincristine
description: Vinca alkaloid from the Madagascar periwinkle that blocks microtubules; used for leukemia and lymphoma.

name: Letrozole
description: Aromatase inhibitor that blocks estrogen synthesis; used for hormone-sensitive breast cancer.

name: Anastrozole
description: Nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor for hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer after menopause.

name: Sildenafil
description: PDE5 inhibitor for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension; first studied for angina. Brand Viagra.

name: Tadalafil
description: Long-acting PDE5 inhibitor for erectile dysfunction, enlarged prostate and pulmonary hypertension.

name: Finasteride
description: 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor that lowers DHT; used for enlarged prostate and male pattern hair loss.

name: Tamsulosin
description: Alpha-1A adrenergic blocker that relaxes prostate muscle to ease urination in prostate enlargement.

name: Oxybutynin
description: Antimuscarinic drug that relaxes bladder muscle; used for overactive bladder.

name: Allopurinol
description: Xanthine oxidase inhibitor that lowers uric acid to prevent gout; from Elion and Hitchings' work.

name: Colchicine
description: Alkaloid from autumn crocus that blocks microtubules; used for gout attacks and familial Mediterranean fever.

name: Ethinylestradiol
description: Synthetic orally active estrogen (1938), the estrogen in most combined contraceptive pills.

name: Levonorgestrel
description: Synthetic progestin used in contraceptive pills, intrauterine devices and emergency contraception.

name: Mifepristone
description: Progesterone and glucocorticoid receptor antagonist used in medical abortion and Cushing's syndrome.

name: Thalidomide
description: Sedative withdrawn in 1961 after causing birth defects; now used for myeloma and leprosy complications.

name: Isotretinoin
description: Retinoid taken orally for severe acne; strictly controlled because it causes birth defects.

name: Minoxidil
description: Vasodilator first used for hypertension; its hair growth side effect led to topical use for hair loss.

name: Latanoprost
description: Prostaglandin F2-alpha analog eye drop that lowers eye pressure in glaucoma.

name: Tetrodotoxin
description: Pufferfish toxin made by symbiotic bacteria; blocks nerve sodium channels and is a key research tool.

name: Strychnine
description: Alkaloid from Strychnos nux-vomica seeds that blocks glycine receptors, causing muscle convulsions.

name: Aconitine
description: Alkaloid of monkshood (Aconitum) that holds sodium channels open, disturbing heart and nerve function.

name: Alpha-amanitin
description: Cyclic peptide of the death cap mushroom that blocks RNA polymerase II, causing liver failure.

name: Phalloidin
description: Bicyclic peptide of the death cap mushroom that binds actin filaments; used to stain them in microscopy.

name: Muscarine
description: Alkaloid from Inocybe and Clitocybe mushrooms that activates muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.

name: Ibotenic acid
description: Glutamate-like amino acid of fly agaric mushrooms that activates glutamate receptors.

name: Muscimol
description: GABA-A receptor agonist in fly agaric mushrooms, formed when ibotenic acid loses carbon dioxide.

name: Aflatoxin B1
description: Mycotoxin of Aspergillus molds on stored grain and nuts; a potent liver carcinogen.

name: Ochratoxin A
description: Mycotoxin from Aspergillus and Penicillium molds in cereals and coffee; damages the kidneys.

name: Patulin
description: Mycotoxin of Penicillium expansum found in rotting apples and apple juice; regulated in foods.

name: Deoxynivalenol
description: Vomitoxin, a trichothecene mycotoxin from Fusarium on wheat and maize that blocks protein synthesis.

name: Fumonisin B1
description: Fusarium mycotoxin common in maize that disrupts sphingolipid metabolism.

name: Ergotamine
description: Ergot alkaloid of Claviceps fungus on rye, cause of medieval ergotism; also a migraine medicine.

name: Alpha-solanine
description: Glycoalkaloid in green potato skins and sprouts that disrupts cell membranes and inhibits cholinesterase.

name: Digitoxin
description: Cardiac glycoside of purple foxglove that inhibits the sodium-potassium pump in heart muscle.

name: Oleandrin
description: Cardiac glycoside in all parts of the oleander shrub; inhibits the sodium-potassium pump.

name: Batrachotoxin
description: Steroidal alkaloid in the skin of Colombian poison dart frogs that holds sodium channels open.

name: Tubocurarine
description: Alkaloid of curare arrow poison that blocks nicotinic receptors at muscles; once used in anesthesia.

name: Coniine
description: Piperidine alkaloid of poison hemlock that blocks nicotinic receptors; it killed Socrates in 399 BC.

name: Cicutoxin
description: Polyacetylene alcohol of water hemlock that blocks GABA-A receptors, causing seizures.

name: Grayanotoxin I
description: Diterpene of rhododendron nectar, cause of mad honey poisoning; holds sodium channels open.

name: Microcystin-LR
description: Cyclic peptide toxin of cyanobacterial blooms in lakes that inhibits protein phosphatases in the liver.

name: Anatoxin-a
description: Cyanobacterial alkaloid in freshwater blooms that strongly activates nicotinic receptors; harms dogs.

name: Domoic acid
description: Diatom toxin that builds up in shellfish and activates glutamate receptors; causes amnesic shellfish poisoning.

name: Brevetoxin B
description: Polyether toxin of red tide algae Karenia brevis that opens sodium channels; causes shellfish poisoning.

name: Okadaic acid
description: Polyether toxin of dinoflagellates that inhibits protein phosphatases; causes diarrhetic shellfish poisoning.

name: Cantharidin
description: Terpenoid secreted by blister beetles that inhibits protein phosphatases and blisters skin; used for warts.

name: TCDD
description: The most toxic dioxin, an industrial combustion pollutant that acts through the aryl hydrocarbon receptor.

name: Methylmercury
description: Organic mercury made by microbes in sediments; builds up in fish and caused Minamata disease in Japan.

name: Amygdalin
description: Cyanogenic glycoside in bitter almond and apricot kernels that releases hydrogen cyanide when digested.

name: Caffeine
description: Purine alkaloid from coffee, tea and cacao; an adenosine receptor antagonist and mild stimulant.

name: Theobromine
description: Dimethylxanthine that is the main alkaloid of cacao beans; a close structural relative of caffeine.

name: Theophylline
description: Dimethylxanthine found in tea leaves; it relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and has been used for asthma.

name: Nicotine
description: Pyridine-pyrrolidine alkaloid of the tobacco plant that acts on nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.

name: Cocaine
description: Tropane alkaloid from coca leaves; historically the first local anesthetic used in eye surgery.

name: Atropine
description: Racemic tropane alkaloid from deadly nightshade that blocks muscarinic acetylcholine receptors.

name: Hyoscyamine
description: The levorotatory tropane alkaloid of Solanaceae plants; atropine is its racemic form.

name: Scopolamine
description: Tropane alkaloid with an epoxide bridge, found in henbane and Datura; an antimuscarinic agent.

name: Quinine
description: Cinchona bark alkaloid with a quinoline core; the historic antimalarial and the bitter taste of tonic water.

name: Quinidine
description: Diastereomer of quinine from cinchona bark, used in medicine as an antiarrhythmic agent.

name: Cinchonine
description: Cinchona alkaloid lacking quinine's methoxy group; used as a chiral auxiliary in resolutions.

name: Papaverine
description: Benzylisoquinoline alkaloid from the opium poppy that relaxes smooth muscle; it has no narcotic action.

name: Noscapine
description: Phthalideisoquinoline alkaloid from the opium poppy, used as a cough suppressant without narcotic effects.

name: Berberine
description: Bright yellow quaternary protoberberine alkaloid from goldenseal and barberry roots.

name: Sanguinarine
description: Quaternary benzophenanthridine alkaloid from bloodroot, named for the red-orange sap of the plant.

name: Chelidonine
description: Benzophenanthridine alkaloid from greater celandine, a plant with bright orange latex.

name: Capsaicin
description: Vanilloid amide that gives chili peppers their heat by activating the TRPV1 heat receptor.

name: Piperine
description: Piperidine amide of piperic acid responsible for the pungency of black pepper.

name: Ephedrine
description: Phenethylamine alkaloid from Ephedra plants that acts on adrenergic receptors; used as a decongestant.

name: Mescaline
description: Trimethoxy phenethylamine alkaloid found in the peyote and San Pedro cacti.

name: Psilocybin
description: Phosphorylated tryptamine alkaloid produced by several species of Psilocybe mushrooms.

name: LSD
description: Semisynthetic diethylamide of lysergic acid, an ergoline first prepared by Albert Hofmann in 1938.

name: Reserpine
description: Indole alkaloid from Indian snakeroot that depletes stored monoamines; an early antihypertensive.

name: Vinblastine
description: Dimeric indole alkaloid from the Madagascar periwinkle that binds tubulin; an anticancer agent.

name: Camptothecin
description: Pentacyclic quinoline alkaloid from the happy tree that inhibits DNA topoisomerase I.

name: Brucine
description: Dimethoxy analog of strychnine from the same seeds, often used to resolve racemic acids.

name: Yohimbine
description: Indole alkaloid from the bark of the yohimbe tree; an alpha-2 adrenergic receptor antagonist.

name: Ibogaine
description: Indole alkaloid from the root bark of the African shrub Tabernanthe iboga.

name: Harmine
description: Fluorescent beta-carboline alkaloid from Syrian rue and ayahuasca vine; a monoamine oxidase inhibitor.

name: Harmaline
description: Dihydro beta-carboline alkaloid from Syrian rue seeds, closely related to harmine.

name: Emetine
description: Isoquinoline alkaloid from ipecac root that inhibits protein synthesis; once used against amoebic dysentery.

name: Physostigmine
description: Pyrroloindole alkaloid from the Calabar bean that reversibly inhibits acetylcholinesterase.

name: Galantamine
description: Amaryllidaceae alkaloid from snowdrops that inhibits acetylcholinesterase; used for Alzheimer disease.

name: Huperzine A
description: Lycopodium alkaloid from the club moss Huperzia serrata; a potent acetylcholinesterase inhibitor.

name: Pilocarpine
description: Imidazole alkaloid from jaborandi leaves that stimulates muscarinic receptors; used for glaucoma.

name: Arecoline
description: Tetrahydropyridine ester alkaloid from the areca nut, a muscarinic receptor agonist.

name: Lobeline
description: Piperidine alkaloid from Indian tobacco (Lobelia inflata) that acts on nicotinic receptors.

name: Cytisine
description: Quinolizidine alkaloid from laburnum seeds, a partial agonist at nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.

name: Sparteine
description: Tetracyclic quinolizidine alkaloid from broom and lupins, used as a chiral ligand in synthesis.

name: Lupinine
description: Bicyclic quinolizidine alkaloid from lupin seeds with a primary alcohol side group.

name: Anabasine
description: Pyridine-piperidine alkaloid from tree tobacco, an isomer-like relative of nicotine.

name: Tomatine
description: Steroidal glycoalkaloid from tomato leaves and green fruit with a four-sugar chain.

name: Staurosporine
description: Indolocarbazole alkaloid from Streptomyces bacteria; a broad inhibitor of protein kinases.

name: Artemisinin
description: Sesquiterpene lactone with an endoperoxide bridge from sweet wormwood; the base of modern antimalarials.

name: Salicin
description: Glucoside of salicyl alcohol from willow bark; the natural forerunner of aspirin.

name: Resveratrol
description: Stilbene polyphenol made by grapes and other plants in response to stress and fungal attack.

name: Quercetin
description: Flavonol with five hydroxyl groups, common in onions, apples and capers.

name: Kaempferol
description: Flavonol found in tea, kale and beans; it has one fewer hydroxyl group than quercetin.

name: Myricetin
description: Flavonol with six hydroxyl groups, found in berries, walnuts and red wine.

name: Apigenin
description: Flavone found in parsley, celery and chamomile flowers.

name: Luteolin
description: Yellow flavone found in celery, thyme and green peppers; a catechol analog of apigenin.

name: Naringenin
description: Flavanone aglycone responsible for part of the bitterness of grapefruit.
