name: Hesperidin
description: Flavanone glycoside abundant in the peel of oranges and lemons.

name: Rutin
description: Glycoside of quercetin with the disaccharide rutinose, found in buckwheat and asparagus.

name: Taxifolin
description: Dihydroflavonol, also called dihydroquercetin, found in Siberian larch and milk thistle.

name: Genistein
description: Isoflavone from soybeans whose shape lets it bind estrogen receptors weakly.

name: Daidzein
description: Soy isoflavone that lacks one hydroxyl group of genistein; a precursor of equol in the gut.

name: Catechin
description: Flavan-3-ol monomer of condensed tannins, found in tea, cocoa and grapes.

name: Epicatechin
description: Flavan-3-ol diastereomer of catechin, abundant in cocoa and green tea.

name: Epigallocatechin gallate
description: Gallate ester of epigallocatechin; the most abundant catechin in green tea.

name: Curcumin
description: Yellow diarylheptanoid from turmeric root; it exists as keto and enol tautomers.

name: Ellagic acid
description: Planar dilactone of hexahydroxydiphenic acid found in raspberries, pomegranates and oak.

name: Gallic acid
description: Trihydroxybenzoic acid from oak galls and tea; a building block of hydrolysable tannins.

name: Shikimic acid
description: Cyclohexene carboxylic acid from star anise; the key intermediate in aromatic amino acid biosynthesis.

name: Podophyllotoxin
description: Aryltetralin lignan from the mayapple root that binds tubulin; parent of etoposide.

name: Cannabidiol
description: Non-intoxicating phytocannabinoid of Cannabis sativa with an open resorcinol ring structure.

name: Tetrahydrocannabinol
description: Main psychoactive phytocannabinoid of Cannabis sativa, a partial agonist at CB1 receptors.

name: Ginkgolide B
description: Cage-like diterpene trilactone from Ginkgo biloba leaves with a tert-butyl group.

name: Forskolin
description: Labdane diterpene from the Indian coleus plant that directly activates adenylyl cyclase.

name: Stevioside
description: Diterpene glycoside from Stevia rebaudiana leaves, about 200 times sweeter than sucrose.

name: Glycyrrhizin
description: Triterpenoid saponin from licorice root that gives licorice its sweet taste.

name: Ginsenoside Rb1
description: Dammarane triterpenoid saponin, the most abundant ginsenoside in Panax ginseng root.

name: Oleanolic acid
description: Pentacyclic triterpenoid acid found in olive leaves and many fruit waxes.

name: Ursolic acid
description: Pentacyclic triterpenoid acid from apple peel wax; an isomer of oleanolic acid.

name: Betulin
description: Lupane triterpene diol that makes up a large part of the white bark of birch trees.

name: Gossypol
description: Yellow polyphenolic binaphthyl aldehyde from cotton seeds with restricted axial rotation.

name: Parthenolide
description: Germacranolide sesquiterpene lactone from feverfew with a reactive alpha-methylene lactone.

name: Triptolide
description: Diterpenoid triepoxide from the thunder god vine, a potent inhibitor of gene transcription.

name: Withaferin A
description: Steroidal lactone (withanolide) from the ashwagandha plant Withania somnifera.

name: Ouabain
description: Cardiac glycoside from Strophanthus seeds, once used as an African arrow poison.

name: Sirolimus
description: Macrolide from Easter Island soil bacteria that inhibits mTOR; also called rapamycin.

name: Tacrolimus
description: Macrolide lactone from Streptomyces tsukubaensis that suppresses T-cell activation via calcineurin.

name: Cyclosporin A
description: Cyclic undecapeptide from a soil fungus with N-methylated residues; an immunosuppressant.

name: Epothilone B
description: Macrolide from myxobacteria that stabilises microtubules much as paclitaxel does.

name: Indigo
description: Blue vat dye from woad and indigo plants, used for denim; its color comes from a cross-conjugated core.

name: Tyrian purple
description: Brominated indigo made by Murex sea snails; the costly imperial purple of antiquity.

name: Indigo carmine
description: Disulfonated indigo that is water soluble; used as a food dye and a medical diagnostic stain.

name: Thioindigo
description: Sulfur analog of indigo with a red-pink color, used as a vat dye and pigment.

name: Alizarin
description: Red anthraquinone dye from madder root; the first natural dye made synthetically, in 1868.

name: Purpurin
description: Trihydroxyanthraquinone red dye that also occurs in madder root alongside alizarin.

name: Quinizarin
description: 1,4-Dihydroxyanthraquinone, an orange-red compound used as an intermediate for dyes.

name: Alizarin red S
description: Sulfonated alizarin used to stain calcium deposits in bone and tissue sections.

name: Mauveine A
description: Main component of mauve, the first synthetic aniline dye, discovered by William Perkin in 1856.

name: Methylene blue
description: Phenothiazinium dye used as a biological stain and a redox indicator.

name: Crystal violet
description: Triarylmethane dye used in the Gram stain to color bacterial cell walls.

name: Malachite green
description: Green triarylmethane dye used to color silk and leather; named for its color, not the mineral.

name: Pararosaniline
description: Magenta triarylmethane dye that is a main component of basic fuchsin and the Schiff reagent.

name: Fluorescein
description: Xanthene dye with bright green fluorescence, used to trace water flow and in eye examinations.

name: Eosin Y
description: Tetrabrominated fluorescein that gives the pink in the hematoxylin and eosin tissue stain.

name: Erythrosine
description: Tetraiodofluorescein used as a cherry-pink food color and dental plaque stain.

name: Rose Bengal
description: Halogenated xanthene dye that makes singlet oxygen under light; used as an eye stain.

name: Rhodamine B
description: Fluorescent xanthene dye with diethylamino groups, used in lasers and as a tracer.

name: Phenolphthalein
description: Acid-base indicator that is colorless in acid and pink above about pH 8.2.

name: Thymol blue
description: Sulfonephthalein indicator with two color changes, red to yellow and yellow to blue.

name: Bromothymol blue
description: Sulfonephthalein indicator that changes from yellow to blue near neutral pH.

name: Bromophenol blue
description: Sulfonephthalein dye used as a pH indicator and as a tracking dye in gel electrophoresis.

name: Phenol red
description: Sulfonephthalein indicator added to cell culture media to show changes in pH.

name: Methyl orange
description: Azo dye indicator that changes from red to yellow between pH 3.1 and 4.4.

name: Methyl red
description: Azo dye indicator, red below pH 4.4 and yellow above pH 6.2.

name: Congo red
description: Bis-azo direct dye that binds amyloid fibrils and shows apple-green birefringence.

name: Azobenzene
description: Parent aromatic azo compound that switches between trans and cis forms under light.

name: Aniline yellow
description: The first azo dye, made in 1861; an amino-substituted azobenzene.

name: Sudan I
description: Orange-red azo dye soluble in oils and waxes, used to color solvents and plastics.

name: Sudan III
description: Red bis-azo lysochrome dye used to stain lipids and fats in tissue sections.

name: Para red
description: Red azo pigment made from p-nitroaniline and 2-naphthol; one of the first synthetic pigments.

name: Orange II
description: Sulfonated azo dye used to color wool, paper and leather.

name: Tartrazine
description: Lemon-yellow pyrazolone azo dye used as a food color, labelled E102.

name: Sunset yellow FCF
description: Orange azo food dye, labelled E110, used in drinks and confectionery.

name: Allura red AC
description: Red azo food dye, labelled E129, widely used in soft drinks and sweets.

name: Brilliant blue FCF
description: Blue triarylmethane food dye, labelled E133, used in drinks and ice cream.

name: Coomassie brilliant blue G-250
description: Triarylmethane dye that binds proteins; the basis of the Bradford protein assay.

name: Phthalocyanine
description: Metal-free macrocycle of four isoindole units; the parent of a large family of blue-green pigments.

name: Copper phthalocyanine
description: Copper complex of phthalocyanine; the very stable Phthalo Blue pigment of paints and inks.

name: Quinacridone
description: Pentacyclic pigment with red to violet colors, used in automotive paints for its stability.

name: Porphine
description: Parent macrocycle of all porphyrins: four pyrrole rings joined by methine bridges.

name: Lycopene
description: Acyclic red carotenoid of tomatoes with eleven conjugated double bonds.

name: Astaxanthin
description: Keto-carotenoid that gives salmon, shrimp and flamingos their pink-red color.

name: Lutein
description: Yellow xanthophyll carotenoid concentrated in the macula of the human retina.

name: Zeaxanthin
description: Xanthophyll carotenoid that gives maize its yellow color; an isomer of lutein.

name: Bixin
description: Apocarotenoid methyl ester from annatto seeds, used to color cheese and butter orange.

name: Crocin
description: Water-soluble digentiobiose ester of crocetin that gives saffron its yellow color.

name: Cyanidin
description: Anthocyanidin pigment of red berries and red cabbage; its color changes with pH.

name: Delphinidin
description: Blue-purple anthocyanidin with three B-ring hydroxyl groups, found in violas and grapes.

name: Pelargonidin
description: Orange-red anthocyanidin of strawberries and geraniums with one B-ring hydroxyl group.

name: Malvidin
description: Dimethoxy anthocyanidin that gives most of the color of red wine.

name: Betanin
description: Red-violet betacyanin glucoside from beetroot, used as a food color (E162).

name: Carminic acid
description: Red anthraquinone C-glycoside from cochineal insects; the source of carmine.

name: Lawsone
description: Red-orange naphthoquinone in henna leaves that binds keratin in skin and hair.

name: Hematoxylin
description: Logwood tree compound that oxidizes to hematein, the nuclear stain in H and E histology.

name: Brazilin
description: Natural red dye from brazilwood that oxidizes to the colored compound brazilein.

name: Safranin O
description: Red phenazinium dye used as the counterstain in the Gram stain.

name: Acridine orange
description: Cationic acridine dye that stains DNA green and RNA red-orange under blue light.

name: Ethidium bromide
description: Phenanthridinium dye that intercalates into DNA; a classic stain for nucleic acids in gels.

name: DAPI
description: Blue fluorescent dye that binds the minor groove of AT-rich DNA, used to stain cell nuclei.

name: Hoechst 33258
description: Bis-benzimidazole dye that binds the DNA minor groove and fluoresces blue.

name: Nile red
description: Benzophenoxazone dye that fluoresces strongly in fat droplets and weakly in water.

name: Nile blue
description: Benzophenoxazinium dye used to stain cell nuclei and lipids in histology.

name: Coumarin 1
description: Blue-emitting coumarin laser dye with a 7-diethylamino donor group.

name: BODIPY
description: Boron difluoride dipyrromethene core of a family of bright, sharp-emitting fluorescent dyes.

name: Indocyanine green
description: Near-infrared cyanine dye used in medical imaging of blood flow and liver function.

name: Xylene cyanol FF
description: Triarylmethane tracking dye used to follow DNA during gel electrophoresis.

name: Emodin
description: Orange trihydroxyanthraquinone from rhubarb, buckthorn and some lichens.

name: Benzene
description: Prototype aromatic ring: six carbons with six delocalized pi electrons and equal bond lengths.

name: Naphthalene
description: Two fused benzene rings; the simplest polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon and the odor of mothballs.

name: Anthracene
description: Three linearly fused rings; a blue-fluorescent solid used in organic semiconductors.

name: Phenanthrene
description: Three angularly fused benzene rings; the carbon skeleton of steroids and morphinans.

name: Tetracene
description: Four linearly fused rings; an orange organic semiconductor that shows singlet fission.

name: Pentacene
description: Five linearly fused rings; a benchmark p-type semiconductor for organic transistors.

name: Chrysene
description: Four-ring PAH with a zigzag shape, found in coal tar and creosote.

name: Triphenylene
description: Disc-shaped four-ring PAH with three outer rings around a central ring; it forms discotic liquid crystals.

name: Pyrene
description: Four-ring peri-fused PAH known for its excimer fluorescence.

name: Fluoranthene
description: Non-alternant PAH with a five-membered ring linking naphthalene and benzene units.

name: Benzo[a]pyrene
description: Five-ring PAH from incomplete combustion, a known carcinogen in smoke and tar.

name: Perylene
description: Five-ring PAH and the core of perylene diimide dyes and pigments.

name: Coronene
description: Seven-ring disc-shaped PAH sometimes called superbenzene; a small graphene fragment.

name: Corannulene
description: Bowl-shaped PAH with five benzene rings around a pentagon; a C60 cap fragment.

name: [6]Helicene
description: Six ortho-fused benzene rings that coil into a helix, so the molecule is chiral.

name: Azulene
description: Blue non-benzenoid aromatic hydrocarbon of fused five- and seven-membered rings with a dipole.

name: Biphenyl
description: Two phenyl rings joined by a single bond, twisted about 44 degrees in the gas phase.

name: Fluorene
description: Biphenyl bridged by a CH2 group into a planar tricycle; it fluoresces violet.

name: Indene
description: Benzene fused to cyclopentene; a coal tar component used to make resins.

name: Acenaphthylene
description: Naphthalene with an etheno bridge across the peri positions, giving a five-membered ring.

name: Triptycene
description: Three benzene rings fixed like paddles around a bicyclic core with D3h symmetry.

name: Hexamethylbenzene
description: Benzene with six methyl groups; its X-ray structure in 1929 proved the ring is flat.

name: Mesitylene
description: 1,3,5-Trimethylbenzene, a symmetric aromatic used as a solvent and ligand precursor.

name: o-Xylene
description: 1,2-Dimethylbenzene, the feedstock for phthalic anhydride.

name: m-Xylene
description: 1,3-Dimethylbenzene, used to make isophthalic acid for resins.

name: p-Xylene
description: 1,4-Dimethylbenzene, oxidized on a large scale to terephthalic acid for PET.

name: Aniline
description: Aminobenzene; the parent aromatic amine and the base of the first synthetic dyes.

name: Hexafluorobenzene
description: Perfluorinated benzene whose reversed quadrupole lets it stack face to face with benzene.

name: Borazine
description: B3N3H6 ring isoelectronic with benzene, often called inorganic benzene.

name: Cyclooctatetraene
description: Eight-membered ring with 8 pi electrons; it adopts a tub shape and is not aromatic.

name: Cyclopentadiene
description: Non-aromatic diene whose deprotonated anion is aromatic; it dimerizes at room temperature.

name: [18]Annulene
description: Eighteen-membered ring with 18 pi electrons; a large aromatic ring with inner hydrogens.

name: Pyridine
description: Six-membered aromatic ring with one nitrogen; a weak base and common solvent.

name: Pyrimidine
description: Diazine with nitrogens at the 1 and 3 positions; the core of cytosine, thymine and uracil.

name: Pyrazine
description: Diazine with nitrogens in the 1 and 4 positions; alkyl pyrazines give roasted aromas.

name: Pyridazine
description: Diazine with adjacent nitrogens at the 1 and 2 positions; a polar aromatic heterocycle.

name: 1,3,5-Triazine
description: Six-membered ring with three alternating nitrogens; the core of melamine.

name: Pyrrole
description: Five-membered aromatic ring with an NH group; the building block of porphyrins.

name: Furan
description: Five-membered aromatic ring with an oxygen atom, made from bran-derived furfural.

name: Thiophene
description: Five-membered aromatic sulfur heterocycle and the repeat unit of polythiophene conductors.

name: Imidazole
description: Five-membered ring with two nitrogens; the side chain of histidine.

name: Pyrazole
description: Five-membered aromatic ring with two adjacent nitrogen atoms.

name: Oxazole
description: Five-membered aromatic ring with oxygen and nitrogen in the 1 and 3 positions.

name: Thiazole
description: Five-membered aromatic ring with sulfur and nitrogen; it occurs in thiamine.

name: Indole
description: Benzene fused to pyrrole; the core of tryptophan, serotonin and many alkaloids.

name: Benzofuran
description: Benzene fused to furan, found in coal tar and many natural products.

name: Benzothiophene
description: Benzene fused to thiophene; it occurs in petroleum and in some drug molecules.

name: Quinoline
description: Benzene fused to pyridine; the core of quinine and many antimalarials.

name: Isoquinoline
description: Benzo-fused pyridine isomer of quinoline; the core of papaverine and berberine.

name: Acridine
description: Anthracene analog with a central nitrogen; the parent of acridine dyes.

name: Phenazine
description: Dibenzopyrazine; bacteria make colored phenazine pigments such as pyocyanin.

name: Carbazole
description: Dibenzopyrrole tricycle used in hole-transport materials for OLEDs.

name: Dibenzofuran
description: Two benzene rings fused to a central furan ring; the parent of polychlorinated dibenzofurans.

name: Purine
description: Fused pyrimidine and imidazole rings; the parent of adenine and guanine.

name: Pteridine
description: Fused pyrimidine and pyrazine rings; the core of folic acid and biopterin.

name: Buckminsterfullerene
description: C60 cage of 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons in the pattern of a football; found in 1985.

name: Fullerene C70
description: C70 cage shaped like a rugby ball, the second most abundant fullerene in carbon soot.

name: Hexabenzocoronene
description: Large disc-shaped PAH of 13 rings, a model fragment of a graphene sheet.

name: [10]Cycloparaphenylene
description: Hoop of ten para-linked benzene rings, the shortest segment of an armchair carbon nanotube.

name: Cubane
description: C8H8 hydrocarbon with eight carbons at the corners of a cube and 90 degree bond angles.

name: Adamantane
description: C10H16 cage that is the smallest repeat unit of the diamond lattice.

name: Diamantane
description: Two face-fused adamantane cages; the second member of the diamondoid series.

name: Triamantane
description: Three fused adamantane cages; a diamondoid found in petroleum condensates.

name: Dodecahedrane
description: C20H20 hydrocarbon with twenty carbons at the vertices of a regular dodecahedron.

name: Prismane
description: C6H6 valence isomer of benzene with carbons at the corners of a triangular prism.

name: Twistane
description: Chiral C10H16 cage with all six-membered rings in twist-boat shapes.

name: Ferrocene
description: Iron atom sandwiched between two cyclopentadienyl rings; its discovery in 1951 began modern organometallics.

name: Ruthenocene
description: Ruthenium sandwich analog of ferrocene with eclipsed cyclopentadienyl rings.

name: Cobaltocene
description: 19-electron cobalt sandwich compound that is a strong one-electron reducing agent.

name: Bis(benzene)chromium
description: Chromium atom sandwiched between two parallel benzene rings; an 18-electron complex.

name: Titanocene dichloride
description: Bent metallocene of titanium with two chlorides; a precursor of olefin polymerization catalysts.

name: Zirconocene dichloride
description: Bent zirconium metallocene used to make Schwartz's reagent and polymerization catalysts.

name: Cisplatin
description: Square planar cis-diamminedichloroplatinum(II), an anticancer drug that cross-links DNA.

name: Carboplatin
description: Platinum(II) anticancer drug with a cyclobutanedicarboxylate leaving group.

name: Oxaliplatin
description: Platinum(II) anticancer drug with a diaminocyclohexane ligand and an oxalate leaving group.

name: Nickel tetracarbonyl
description: Tetrahedral, very toxic Ni(CO)4, the volatile intermediate of the Mond nickel refining process.

name: Iron pentacarbonyl
description: Trigonal bipyramidal Fe(CO)5, a yellow liquid and a source of iron nanoparticles.

name: Chromium hexacarbonyl
description: Octahedral Cr(CO)6, a stable white solid that obeys the 18-electron rule.

name: Molybdenum hexacarbonyl
description: Octahedral Mo(CO)6, a volatile solid used as a molybdenum source in synthesis.

name: Tungsten hexacarbonyl
description: Octahedral W(CO)6, used to deposit tungsten films by decomposition.

name: Dicobalt octacarbonyl
description: Co2(CO)8 with bridging carbonyls, a catalyst for hydroformylation of alkenes.

name: Dimanganese decacarbonyl
description: Mn2(CO)10, two Mn(CO)5 units joined by an unsupported metal-metal bond.

name: Wilkinson's catalyst
description: Square planar rhodium(I) complex that catalyzes the hydrogenation of alkenes.

name: Vaska's complex
description: Square planar iridium(I) complex that binds O2 and H2 reversibly by oxidative addition.

name: Tetrakis(triphenylphosphine)palladium(0)
description: Tetrahedral Pd(0) complex widely used as a catalyst for Suzuki and Stille coupling.

name: Palladium(II) acetate
description: Trimeric palladium carboxylate used as a catalyst precursor for cross-coupling reactions.

name: Grubbs catalyst (1st generation)
description: Ruthenium benzylidene complex with two tricyclohexylphosphines that catalyzes olefin metathesis.

name: Tris(bipyridine)ruthenium(II) chloride
description: Octahedral, chiral ruthenium complex with orange luminescence, used in photoredox catalysis.

name: Trimethylaluminium
description: Pyrophoric organoaluminium that exists as a dimer with bridging methyl groups.

name: Tetraethyllead
description: Tetrahedral organolead compound formerly added to gasoline as an antiknock agent.

name: Methylmagnesium bromide
description: Simple Grignard reagent that adds methyl groups to carbonyl compounds.

name: n-Butyllithium
description: Organolithium reagent used as a strong base; it forms hexamers in hydrocarbon solvents.

name: Diethylzinc
description: Linear, pyrophoric organozinc compound used in the Simmons-Smith cyclopropanation.

name: Tetramethylsilane
description: Tetrahedral Si(CH3)4, the zero reference for 1H and 13C NMR chemical shifts.

name: Hexamethyldisiloxane
description: Two trimethylsilyl groups joined by oxygen with a wide Si-O-Si angle; a simple silicone fluid.

name: Octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane
description: Cyclic siloxane D4, an eight-membered Si-O ring used to make silicone polymers.

name: Boric acid
description: Trigonal planar B(OH)3, a weak Lewis acid that forms layered hydrogen-bonded sheets.

name: Diborane
description: B2H6 with two three-center two-electron B-H-B bridge bonds.

name: Ammonia borane
description: H3N-BH3 Lewis adduct studied as a solid hydrogen storage material.

name: Trimethylborane
description: Trigonal planar B(CH3)3, a Lewis acid with an empty boron p orbital.

name: Aluminium chloride
description: Trigonal planar AlCl3 monomer, a strong Lewis acid catalyst for Friedel-Crafts reactions.

name: Silane
description: Tetrahedral SiH4, a pyrophoric gas used to deposit silicon in chip fabrication.

name: Silicon tetrachloride
description: Tetrahedral SiCl4, an intermediate in making high-purity silicon and fused silica.

name: Titanium tetrachloride
description: Tetrahedral TiCl4 liquid that fumes in moist air; used to make titanium metal and TiO2.

name: Phosphorus pentachloride
description: Trigonal bipyramidal PCl5 in the gas phase; a chlorinating reagent.

name: Phosphorus pentafluoride
description: Trigonal bipyramidal PF5 whose axial and equatorial fluorines exchange by Berry pseudorotation.

name: Sulfur tetrafluoride
description: Seesaw-shaped SF4 with one lone pair; a reagent that converts C=O groups to CF2.

name: Chlorine trifluoride
description: T-shaped ClF3 with two lone pairs, an extremely reactive fluorinating agent.

name: Bromine trifluoride
description: T-shaped BrF3, a fluorinating liquid that conducts electricity by self-ionization.

name: Iodine pentafluoride
description: Square pyramidal IF5 with one lone pair below the base of the pyramid.

name: Iodine heptafluoride
description: Pentagonal bipyramidal IF7, a rare example of seven-coordinate main group geometry.

name: Xenon difluoride
description: Linear XeF2 with three equatorial lone pairs; a stable noble gas compound.

name: Xenon tetrafluoride
description: Square planar XeF4 with two lone pairs above and below the plane.

name: Xenon hexafluoride
description: XeF6 with a distorted octahedral shape caused by a stereochemically active lone pair.

name: Uranium hexafluoride
description: Octahedral, volatile UF6, used in the gas centrifuge enrichment of uranium.

name: Osmium tetroxide
description: Tetrahedral OsO4, a volatile and toxic oxidant that converts alkenes to cis-diols.

name: Chromyl chloride
description: Tetrahedral CrO2Cl2, a dark red liquid used in the Etard oxidation.

name: Potassium permanganate
description: Purple salt of the tetrahedral MnO4- ion, a strong oxidizing agent.

name: Potassium dichromate
description: Orange salt of the Cr2O7 2- ion, two CrO4 tetrahedra sharing one oxygen.

name: Sulfuric acid
description: Tetrahedral H2SO4, the most produced industrial chemical and a strong diprotic acid.

name: Nitric acid
description: Planar HNO3 with a resonance-delocalized nitro group; a strong oxidizing acid.

name: Phosphoric acid
description: Tetrahedral H3PO4, a triprotic acid used in fertilizers and soft drinks.

name: Perchloric acid
description: Tetrahedral HClO4, one of the strongest common mineral acids.

name: Hydrogen peroxide
description: H2O2 with a skewed O-O bond and a dihedral angle of about 111 degrees.

name: Cyclooctasulfur
description: S8 crown-shaped ring, the most stable form of elemental sulfur.

name: Phosphorus pentoxide
description: P4O10 cage built on a P4 tetrahedron with bridging and terminal oxygens; a strong drying agent.

name: EDTA
description: Hexadentate chelating agent that wraps around metal ions; used in water softening and analysis.

name: Hemin
description: Iron(III) protoporphyrin IX chloride, the oxidized heme group of hemoglobin.

name: Vanillin
description: Phenolic aldehyde that is the main flavour compound of vanilla beans.

name: Ethyl vanillin
description: Synthetic analog of vanillin with an ethoxy group, about three times stronger in odor.

name: Cinnamaldehyde
description: Unsaturated aromatic aldehyde that gives cinnamon bark its flavour and odor.

name: Eugenol
description: Allyl guaiacol that is the main aroma compound of clove oil.

name: Menthol
description: Cyclic monoterpene alcohol from peppermint that activates the cold receptor TRPM8.

name: Menthone
description: Monoterpene ketone of peppermint oil with a minty, slightly woody odor.

name: (R)-Limonene
description: Monoterpene that gives orange and lemon peel oil its citrus odor.

name: (R)-Carvone
description: The (R)-(-) enantiomer of carvone, with the odor of spearmint.

name: (S)-Carvone
description: The (S)-(+) enantiomer of carvone, with the odor of caraway and dill seed.

name: Geranial
description: The E isomer of citral, a monoterpene aldehyde with a strong lemon odor.

name: Linalool
description: Floral monoterpene alcohol found in lavender, coriander and many flowers.

name: Geraniol
description: Monoterpene alcohol with a rose-like odor, found in rose and palmarosa oils.

name: Nerol
description: Z isomer of geraniol with a sweet rose odor, found in neroli oil.

name: Citronellal
description: Monoterpene aldehyde with a lemony odor, the main component of citronella oil.

name: Myrcene
description: Acyclic monoterpene with a balsamic odor, abundant in hops and bay leaves.

name: alpha-Pinene
description: Bicyclic monoterpene with an endocyclic double bond; the main odor of pine resin.

name: beta-Pinene
description: Bicyclic monoterpene with an exocyclic double bond; found in turpentine and hops.

name: 1,8-Cineole
description: Bicyclic ether monoterpene that gives eucalyptus oil its camphor-like odor.

name: Camphor
description: Bicyclic monoterpene ketone from the camphor laurel with a cooling, medicinal odor.

name: Thymol
description: Isopropyl methyl phenol that is the main aroma compound of thyme oil.

name: Carvacrol
description: Isomer of thymol that gives oregano its warm, pungent odor.

name: Anethole
description: Phenylpropene with a sweet licorice odor, found in anise, star anise and fennel.

name: Cuminaldehyde
description: Isopropyl benzaldehyde that is the main odor compound of cumin seed.

name: Benzaldehyde
description: Simplest aromatic aldehyde, with the odor of bitter almonds and cherries.

name: Piperonal
description: Methylenedioxy benzaldehyde, also called heliotropin, with a cherry-vanilla floral odor.

name: Coumarin
description: Benzopyrone with a sweet hay odor, found in tonka beans and sweet clover.

name: Raspberry ketone
description: Phenolic butanone that is the main aroma compound of raspberries.

name: Methyl salicylate
description: Methyl ester of salicylic acid that gives wintergreen its minty odor.

name: Methyl anthranilate
description: Amino benzoate ester with the odor of Concord grapes, also found in orange blossom.

name: Benzyl acetate
description: Ester with a sweet floral odor, the main component of jasmine absolute.

name: 2-Phenylethanol
description: Aromatic alcohol with a soft rose odor, found in roses and many fermented foods.

name: Isoamyl acetate
description: Ester with a strong banana and pear-drop odor, also an alarm pheromone of honeybees.

name: Ethyl butyrate
description: Fruity ester with a pineapple odor, used widely in fruit flavours.

name: gamma-Decalactone
description: Five-membered lactone with a strong peach odor, found in peaches and apricots.

name: delta-Decalactone
description: Six-membered lactone with a creamy coconut and milk odor, found in butter.

name: Maltol
description: Pyranone from larch bark and roasted malt with a caramel odor; used as a flavour enhancer.

name: Ethyl maltol
description: Ethyl analog of maltol with a stronger caramel and cotton candy odor.

name: Furaneol
description: Furanone with a caramel-strawberry odor, a key aroma of strawberries and pineapple.

name: Sotolon
description: Furanone with a fenugreek and maple syrup odor at low concentration.

name: Diacetyl
description: Vicinal diketone that gives butter its typical odor; also a fermentation byproduct.

name: Acetoin
description: Hydroxy ketone with a buttery odor, made by yeast and bacteria during fermentation.

name: 2-Acetyl-1-pyrroline
description: Cyclic imine that gives jasmine rice, pandan and bread crust their aroma.

name: 2-Isobutyl-3-methoxypyrazine
description: Pyrazine with a green bell pepper odor detectable at parts per trillion.

name: Nootkatone
description: Sesquiterpene ketone that is a main aroma compound of grapefruit.

name: Rotundone
description: Sesquiterpene ketone that gives black pepper and Syrah wine their peppery note.

name: alpha-Ionone
description: Cyclic terpenoid ketone with a violet odor; it has the ring double bond in the alpha position.

name: beta-Ionone
description: Carotenoid-derived ketone with a violet and woody odor, found in roses and raspberries.

name: beta-Damascenone
description: Rose ketone with a cooked apple odor, important in rose oil and wine at trace levels.

name: cis-Jasmone
description: Cyclopentenone with a fruity jasmine odor, found in jasmine flowers.

name: Hedione
description: Methyl dihydrojasmonate, a light jasmine-like aroma chemical used in many perfumes.

name: Muscone
description: 15-membered macrocyclic ketone that is the main odor compound of natural musk.

name: Civetone
description: 17-membered unsaturated macrocyclic ketone with a musky odor, first found in civet.

name: Ambroxide
description: Tricyclic ether with the woody, amber odor of ambergris; made from sclareol.

name: Galaxolide
description: Polycyclic musk with a clean, sweet odor, widely used in laundry products.

name: Iso E Super
description: Woody, cedar-like aroma chemical with a velvety odor, used in many modern perfumes.

name: Geosmin
description: Bicyclic alcohol made by soil bacteria that gives the earthy odor after rain.

name: 2-Methylisoborneol
description: Terpene alcohol from soil microbes that gives water and fish a musty, earthy taint.

name: 1-Octen-3-ol
description: Unsaturated alcohol with a mushroom odor, sometimes called mushroom alcohol.

name: Hexanal
description: Six-carbon aldehyde with a cut grass odor, formed when plant fatty acids break down.

name: cis-3-Hexen-1-ol
description: Leaf alcohol with the intense odor of freshly cut green grass and leaves.

name: Allicin
description: Thiosulfinate formed when garlic is crushed; it gives fresh garlic its pungent odor.

name: Allyl isothiocyanate
description: Pungent isothiocyanate of mustard, horseradish and wasabi made from sinigrin.

name: Aspartame
description: Methyl ester of the aspartyl-phenylalanine dipeptide, about 200 times sweeter than sucrose.

name: Neotame
description: N-alkylated derivative of aspartame, about 7,000 to 13,000 times sweeter than sucrose.

name: Sucralose
description: Trichlorinated sucrose derivative about 600 times sweeter than sucrose.

name: Saccharin
description: Benzisothiazolone sulfonamide, the first artificial sweetener, discovered in 1879.

name: Acesulfame
description: Oxathiazinone dioxide sweetener about 200 times sweeter than sucrose, used as its potassium salt.

name: Steviol
description: Diterpene aglycone of the sweet glycosides of Stevia rebaudiana; it is not sweet itself.
